383YE Autumn Equinox Synod judgements.d: No change of doctrine or veto was sought. Statements condemned the sword scholars' obstruction, defended briars and lineaged citizens, and backed the painful ceding of Feroz to the Grendel. Several mandates failed for lack of a greater majority because the Wisdom assembly and sword scholars intervened, including pilgrimages to Zenith and Holberg. Enacted mandates included purifying Holberg's waters at a cost to Highborn businesses, the Crusading Storm order for Highborn armies, efforts to lift Wither the Seed from Brocéliande, and stronger sword scholar support in Urizen. Veikko Bondforger and Astrid Rezia di Tassato became Cardinals of Loyalty and Pride, and the Virtue Fund closed at 39 Thrones, 2 Crowns and 1 Ring.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly named its Champions of Virtue, Love and Glory, backed an Applefel market in Weirwater and urged its knights to keep fighting the vallorn. An enacted Highborn mandate lifted the penalty on Dawnish congregations and gave them extra liao and votes.
n.Druj: Urizen declared the Druj its greatest threat and called for them to be driven from Zenith. Varushka called on its Wagon Raiders to hunt the Druj in Ossium, and the Imperial Orcs invited tribes formerly subjugated by the Druj to join their legions in Skarsind.
n.Grendel: The Brass Coast and the Assembly of the Nine accepted the ceasefire that cedes Feroz to the Grendel for two years of peace. The Freeborn urged corsairs to strike the Drake Island shipyard if the treaty failed, or to help evacuate Feroz if it passed.
n.Highguard: An enacted mandate meant every Highborn business would suffer a one-rank penalty the next season so that Holberg's fouled waters could be purified. Another gave the Highborn armies the Crusading Storm order, while other judgements urged the nation to bear the League's curse and to root out the practice of Unveiling.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orc assembly declared its ambition to claim the Barrens and to become a crusading storm. It sent preachers to the orcs of Ossium, welcomed former Druj tribes into the legions in Skarsind, and asked Reavers to aid freed orcs in Axos, while Consul Skywise Fal was called to inquisition over his ambitions for the Throne.
n.Jotun: Wintermark's assembly rejected the Jotun notion of honour and invited former Jotun thralls home. It also honoured Raknar Ravenstorm's raid on Ikka's Tears and Osric's defeat of the Jotun in Atalaq, while the Marchers urged boat raids on the Jotun in Bregasland.
n.Navarr: An enacted Navarr mandate urged the nation to find the magical might to lift Wither the Seed from Brocéliande. The assembly also denounced agents of Yaw'nagrah, condemned the Arhallogen's alliance with the Druj and honoured Eirwen Brackensong's defence against the vallorn.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn accepted the ceding of Feroz as the lesser evil but vowed it was only waiting and pledged to hold senators and generals to account to retake it. They also urged rebuilding the Justicars, exposing smugglers and translating Sumaah texts at the Zemress seminary.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark prepared to welcome home people held in bondage by the Thule, and two magicians were vindicated over a treaty with the Thule.
n.Urizen: An enacted mandate entrenched support for the sword scholars, opening the way to more of their temples in Morrow and dulling Synod-wide statements in Urizen. The assembly also warned that the Citadel Army was starving, offered disbanded Citadel Guard soldiers homes in other spires and called for improvements to Cargo.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly urged its people to bring the ways of the hearth to the new territory of Ossium and called on the Wagon Raiders to protect it and hunt the Druj there. It also praised its preceptor Yevanshka, and Illya Nikovitch Volkov was appointed Guardian of the Maze of Zoria.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark prepared to welcome thralls returning from the Thule and Jotun, called for a trading hall in Valashal and asked Kallavesa to gather herbs for the head healer. It also added Raknar Ravenstorm to the Book of Heroes and stood with Iron Osric in the drive to reclaim Sermersuaq.

t.Brocéliande: An enacted Navarr mandate urged the nation to find ways to remove the Wither the Seed curse from Brocéliande. Eirwen Brackensong was praised for sending the equivalent of 4,260 troops against its vallorn, and Highborn priests were urged to keep supporting the fight there.
t.Zenith: Urizen's assembly called for the Druj to be driven from Zenith. A General Assembly mandate urging pilgrimage to Zenith was upheld but blocked by the Wisdom assembly and the sword scholars.

383YE Autumn Equinox interlude.d: The Imperial Guerdon stood at 175 Thrones, shared among units supporting the Raid on Ikka's Tears, Green Shield, Red Wind Corsairs, Tusks, Granite Pillar, Strong Reeds and Northern Eagle. Units fighting in Segura earned 5 crowns from the Freeborn. New opportunities included slowing the vallorn in Brocéliande, a stealth raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears and a spy network in Ossium. Fleets faced sanctions on Asavea and Nemoria, the closed Iron Confederacy and Jarmish tariffs, and could also evacuate refugees from Aracossa or Telios. Mandates removed the grey pilgrims' penalties in eight nations, but not in Dawn. Other mandates imposed costs to aid the Sand Fishers, let Tharim feast on Navarr lands, and boosted Varushkan mines and congregations opposing idolatry.

n.Dawn: Dawnish captains received extra rewards for helping to slow the vallorn in Brocéliande. Dawn alone kept the grey pilgrims' penalty of 2 votes and 1 liao on its congregations after its assembly chose a different course.
n.Grendel: Grendel pillaging in Feroz left every resource there 2 ranks down. Any further Grendel raids would now meet protective magic that prevented more losses.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations lost 2 votes and 1 liao because of the Blade of the Pilgrims call to aid Brocéliande. The grey pilgrims' penalty on them was lifted.
n.Imperial Orcs: Following Skywise Rykana's mandate to aid the Sand Fishers, every Imperial Orc congregation, farm, business, herb garden, forest, mine, mana site and fleet suffered a one-rank production penalty until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: any plunder by the Lasambrian Jotun in Segura would have no effect on personal resources, thanks to protective magic.
n.Navarr: Every Navarr herb garden lost 2 random herbs per season for a year under the Blood and Gold mandate. Tharim's feast also struck herb gardens and forests in Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia, though the grey pilgrims' penalty was removed.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn paid 5 crowns to each unit defending Segura, and Freeborn fleet captains who traded suffered a -1 production rank after a privateering mandate. Resources in Feroz were also 2 ranks down from Grendel raids, while the grey pilgrims' penalty was lifted.
n.The League: Holberg's citizens took a one-rank production penalty to aid the Sand Fishers, while congregations in Tassato and Temeschwar gained votes and liao from the Reject False Gods mandate. The grey pilgrims' penalty on League congregations was removed.
n.The Marches: The grey pilgrims' penalty on Marcher congregations was removed. Good Leaf Gardens were created in Upwold in recognition of the Marches' sacrifice against the Liathaven vallorn.
n.Urizen: The grey pilgrims' penalty on Urizeni congregations was lifted. Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod opposed idolatry.
n.Varushka: Varushkan mines and forests produced one rank higher until the Spring Equinox 384YE, and Karsk's congregations gained extra votes and liao. The grey pilgrims' penalty was removed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark captains joining the raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears gained courage and morale worth two extra ranks for two seasons. Hahnmark congregations gained votes and liao, and the grey pilgrims' penalty was lifted.

t.Brocéliande: Military units could help the steadings slow the vallorn's expansion here for a season, while Highborn congregations and Tharim's feast were both committed to the fight for the territory.
t.Feroz: All personal resources in Feroz suffered a 2-rank penalty from earlier Grendel pillaging, but protective magic now guarded against further losses. Its Asavean temple was noted as a symbol of cooperation.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao while the Synod clearly opposed idolatry, as the Asavean architect's buildings there were forcibly redesigned.
t.Hercynia: Every herb garden in Hercynia lost two random herbs and every forest two resources until the Winter Solstice 383YE, as Tharim feasted in return for aiding Brocéliande.
t.Holberg: Every congregation, farm, business, herb garden, forest, mine, mana site and fleet in Holberg suffered a one-rank penalty until the Winter Solstice 383YE to support the Sand Fishers.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk received four extra votes and two extra liao for a year, then the same bonus as the other territories with redesigned buildings.
t.Liathaven: An Imperial spy network continued in Liathaven. Units that had helped remove its vallorn suffered a 2-rank penalty until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
t.Miaren: Herb gardens and forests in Miaren suffered reduced production until the Winter Solstice 383YE because of Tharim's feast.
t.Ossium: The Empire now had a spy network in Ossium, which any military unit could support in return for copies of its reports and maps.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod maintained a clear stance against idolatry.
t.Segura: Units supporting the armies engaged in Segura, namely the Bounders, the Tusks and the Strong Reeds, each received 5 crowns from the Freeborn. Protective magic continued to shield Segura from raids on personal resources.
t.Sermersuaq: Imperial captains could launch a stealthy raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears mithril mine, freeing 50 thralls for every thousand points of strength committed.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate enacted by Rafael Barossa di Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao while the Synod stood against idolatry.
t.Therunin: Herb gardens and forests in Therunin suffered reduced production until the Winter Solstice 383YE as Tharim feasted on them.
t.Upwold: Good Leaf Gardens were created in Upwold to honour the Marches' sacrifice against the Liathaven vallorn, paid for by losses to Navarr herb gardens.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers, the new inhabitants of Misericorde, gained significantly from Imperial Orc and Holberg support, which cemented good relations with the people of the city.

383YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: After the Summer Solstice the Throne and the Imperial Magus vanished, and the Constitutional Court declared both posts vacant. Skathe's agents shattered Sarvos's mirrors and ruined Holmauer Park in Holberg. In Brocéliande the vallorn tide was weathered and driven back, but the Heirs of Terunael are gathering in Therunin, Hercynia and Liathaven. The Grendel advanced in Feroz. The Marchers face the hateful Whittle folk, and Ossium is being settled while its foreign orcs' future is debated. Other news covers the Bourse, the sword scholars' return, the Three Watchers statues, Dawnish troubadours in Highguard, the Hylje, the Briar question, and trade and diplomacy with foreign powers.

n.Dawn: Dawnish troubadours travelled to Highguard to teach glory and love, giving Dawn its own answer to the grey pilgrims. The national assembly is also offered Bourse opportunities, and Dawn is tagged in the Fall of Brocéliande.
n.Druj: The Druj threaten the Sand Fishers in Holberg, and two more of their miasma pillars were found in Ossium. They failed to stop the Temple of the Winds being finished in Morrow.
n.Grendel: The Grendel made significant advances in Feroz. Freeborn corsairs have identified four possible targets for a raid against them.
n.Highguard: Highguard welcomed Dawnish troubadours, and Virtue's Rest was completed, though it needs the proposed White Roads to work at full effect. The Sign of Tamar in Reikos is being lost to the wilderness, and Koboldi carved three giant statues of Highborn soldiers in Urizen.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc preachers have been invited to speak to the foreign orcs of Ossium, some of whom might be moved to Skarsind. The nation faces a range of pressing orc affairs and Bourse opportunities.
n.Jotun: The Marchers continue to bring the Jotun thralls of the Mournwold into their nation, while the Whittle folk refuse to celebrate the Wassail alongside them.
n.Navarr: The curse Wither the Seed now lies on both Liathaven and Brocéliande, and the vallorn was repelled in Brocéliande. The Heirs of Terunael are gathering to drive vallornspawn into a frenzy, and most Navarr remain uneasy about briars despite their assembly's statement.
n.The Brass Coast: The Segura defence scheme may be extended to Feroz after Grendel advances there, and corsairs await a raid target from the Freeborn Assembly. The Zemress seminary was completed.
n.The League: Skathe's curses struck Sarvos and Holberg, Temeschwar was spared direct harm, and Tassato's politicians brought forward proposals. The Imperatrix herself, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, vanished.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly has demanded that the Hate-filled Whittle folk recant as part of efforts to unite with the Mournwold's former Jotun thralls, and a painful next step looms.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov are listed among the foreign orcs bordering the Empire, and an Ambassador to Otkodov is tagged.
n.Urizen: The sword scholars' Temple of the Winds was completed in Morrow, and the Three Watchers statues now honour the Highborn who died defending Urizen. A celestial alignment offers the nation opportunities for transformation.
n.Varushka: Varushkan vales are spreading across newly conquered Ossium, and the national assembly welcomed Imperial Orc preachers there. Varushkans are uneasy about the assembly's call for Loyalty to briars.
n.Wintermark: Suaq bands have reached out to the hylje, and a hylje representative is coming to Anvil to renew oaths of friendship with the people of Wintermark.

t.Brocéliande: The vallorn's peak assault was weathered and driven back, giving a respite. The territory now lies under the long-lasting curse Wither the Seed, and briars there reported peculiar dreams.
t.Feroz: The Grendel have made significant advances here, and there is a proposal to extend the Segura defence scheme to Feroz.
t.Hercynia: The Silent Bell found the Heirs of Terunael gathering in force here, poised to drive vallornspawn into a murderous frenzy.
t.Holberg: A curse from the Hag Queen's agents ruined Holmauer Park, though the citizens see opportunity in the disaster. The Sand Fishers living here are threatened by the Druj.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Belakov, Wolf of Karsk, raised the Varushkan statement welcoming Imperial Orc preachers to Ossium.
t.Liathaven: The territory suffers under Wither the Seed, and the Heirs of Terunael are gathering here. A new weirwood grove has been discovered.
t.Madruga: The Zemress seminary in Calvos was completed, and Sumaah präster intend to supply copies of the exemplar's life and works.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: its citizens are tagged in the Tassato news alongside those of Tassato.
t.Morrow: The sword scholars' Temple of the Winds was completed here. Three immense statues of Highborn soldiers now guard the pass from Morrow to Zenith.
t.Mournwold: The Marchers are working to bring in the Jotun thralls here, while the Hate-filled village of Whittle faces demands to recant or face the consequences.
t.Ossium: A spy network mapped the territory and found two more Druj miasma pillars, and settlement is spreading. The Senate must decide whether its foreign orcs stay or move, and the Bitter Vats in Lomaa burned.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: its orcs are listed among the foreign orcs bordering the Empire, and an Ambassador to Otkodov is tagged.
t.Reikos: The Sign of Tamar is being reclaimed by the wilderness and will be lost by Spring without further action. The White Roads would benefit those building homes here.
t.Sarvos: Skathe's agents shattered every mirror in the city, leaving its people fearing an imminent DOOM. A conjunction leads into the sewers.
t.Segura: Locals' contributions to defence succeeded in drawing military units, though no fighting took place and no more territory was lost.
t.Sermersuaq: Conjunctions arise here, and Suaq bands have discussed the territory's sorry state with the hylje.
t.Skarsind: The foreign orcs of Ossium could be encouraged to move here, escorted by the Eastern Sky, if the Senate so chooses.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: conjunctions this season reach into the wild lands of Spiral.
t.Tassato: Tassato's politicians brought forward proposals on the Imperial Consul, Seren and the Whittle folk.
t.Temeschwar: The Hag Queen's agents did not directly harm the city, but its citizens feel the insult to the League.
t.Therunin: The Heirs of Terunael are gathering in force here to stir the vallornspawn into a frenzy.
t.Zenith: The three Highborn statues carved by koboldi stand guard over the pass from Morrow into Zenith, commemorating the fight against the Druj.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The vallorn's push into Boar's Dell was weathered and driven back.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The vallorn's push into Elerael was weathered and driven back.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park was ruined by a malignant curse unleashed by the Hag Queen's agents.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers of Misericorde are threatened by the Druj, and their fate will sway the orcs of Ossium.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: New Varushkan vales are being established here.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Only the most adventurous settlers are moving into the Drownbark Forest.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Few Varushkans are interested in settling in Echofell.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: New Varushkan vales are being established across the Galath Fields.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Few Varushkans are interested in settling in Nearweald.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Conclave declared that the nest here belongs to Arhallogen, so settlers are advised to avoid the area around its temple.

383YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: Three Marcher armies held Segura without a fight, and the Jotun withdrew from Serra Damata without contesting it. In Feroz, five Imperial armies clashed with Grendel marines, the Naguerro and the Iron Gulls, with heavy losses on both sides; Fontargenta fell and the territory with it. The Grendel took Apstrus and Apulian, so Spiral is no longer Imperial. Over twenty thousand Druj pressed into Utterlund, while the Jotun conquered North Fens and Grey Fens. The Ikka's Tears raid freed two hundred thralls, seized the mithril and collapsed the mine. Brocéliande held, aided by Druj warbands sent by Arhallogen. The Military Council must choose two of four Sentinel Gate opportunities: Bregasland, Brocéliande, Feroz or Holberg.

n.Dawn: Many Dawnish knights errant fought the vallorn in Brocéliande, though some turned away in disgust at fighting beside the Druj. Dawnish champions also formed a creditable part of the raid on Ikka's Tears.
n.Druj: A Druj force of more than twenty thousand invaded Holberg and came close to claiming Utterlund. The Druj still hold Screed and Ossuary in Spiral, while fifty Druj warbands sworn to Arhallogen fought the vallorn and now retreat exposed through Boar's Dell.
n.Grendel: The Grendel conquered Feroz, landed two fresh armies including the Naguerro and the Iron Gulls, and seized the Celesti Lighthouse. They also took Apstrus and Apulian in Spiral, although the Black Plateau took its toll on their troops.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave and the Granite Pillar fought in Feroz, where the Pillar repelled the assault on Mora's Rock. The Valiant Pegasus held Elerael against the vallorn, and Highborn champions joined the raid on Ikka's Tears.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun and the Green Shield marched into Kahraman and found that the Jotun had already withdrawn. Imperial Orc warbands were among the most numerous defenders of Brocéliande, and the nation is helping the Sand Fishers settle in Holberg.
n.Jotun: The Jotun abandoned Serra Damata and made no push in Segura, but under the Southern Bear and the Bear-Who-Swims they conquered North Fens and Grey Fens in Bregasland. They lost a season's mithril and around two hundred thralls when the mine at Ikka's Tears was raided and collapsed.
n.Navarr: Brocéliande's steadings survived the vallorn's worst onslaught, and Dark Ranging may now be freed. The Black Thorns and the Quiet Step fought hard against the Grendel in Feroz.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost Feroz to the Grendel but saw Kahraman made wholly Imperial again and Segura spared further loss. The hakima of Afar are seeking heroes to protect a Night working that could call thousands to fight for Feroz.
n.The League: Holberg was invaded by a vast Druj force. The city's great walls kept its people safe, but the surrounding regions are threatened and fouled by corrupt Spring rain.
n.The Marches: The Tusks, the Bounders and the Strong Reeds held Segura unopposed, but at home the Jotun took two regions of Bregasland. Defiant yeofolk are making a stand at Bill Sabbey, and saving it could rally a Marcher militia.
n.Urizen: Spiral is no longer Imperial and its senator has lost their seat. The Citadel Guard will decline and the Doyen of the Spires' rate of codification has fallen. Urizen warbands supported the Granite Pillar in Feroz.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle helped hold the line in Elerael against the vallorn at a heavy cost. Varushkan engineers helped collapse the mine at Ikka's Tears.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains made the raid on Ikka's Tears a full success, freeing Winterfolk thralls and gaining an advantage in Suaq Fount. The Sussivari Frost Coven's Night magic kept the Jotun from taking more of Bregasland.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: a Corsair general's call to arms recalls the Empire bloodying the Grendel in the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun conquered North Fens and Grey Fens. The territory remains Imperial but will fall if one more region is lost.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn's final, most violent attempt to expand was broken, leaving Boar's Dell, Elerael and the Broch in Navarr hands. Dark Ranging may now be retaken, but every unit that fought here suffered grievous wounds.
t.Feroz: Feroz fell to the Grendel when Fontargenta was taken, and is no longer an Imperial territory. Heavy fighting cost both sides around three thousand dead.
t.Holberg: More than twenty thousand Druj invaded and nearly claimed Utterlund, held back only by the city's walls. They now hunt the Sand Fishers while a foul Spring rain poisons the territory.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Jotun champions raiding out of its Blutgahn marshes help explain why few Bregas live in Grey Fens.
t.Kahraman: Imperial Orc armies relieved Fort Braydon, and the Jotun withdrew from Serra Damata, leaving Kahraman entirely Imperial once more.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro once lived in Kalino before the Iron Confederacy defeated them.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: half the Fist of the Mountains rested here, and its regions are named as army routes into Bregasland.
t.Liathaven: The Black Thorns marched out to Feroz. With Grey Fens lost, Imperial armies can no longer reach West Ranging or Westwood without crossing Jotun-held land or first establishing a new beachhead.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Imperial heroes stopped the Grendel seizing the Scorrero crossing between Madruga and Oranseri.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel set up a command post near a major pass from Spiral into Mareave.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks marched from Mitwold, the breadbasket's bounty is to be spread there, and armies must pass through it to reach Ottermire.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: worried messages from Spiral's remaining citizens reach their cousins in Morrow.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched from Mournwold, and Mournwold orcs offered supplies to the Marchers in Bregasland.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Druj seek to punish the Sand Fishers for leaving Ossium, and the orcs of Ossium will hear how the Empire responds.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: worried messages from Spiral's remaining citizens reach their cousins in Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: freeing Dark Ranging would open safer passage between Reikos and Semmerholm.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun withdrew from Serra Damata back into Reinos.
t.Segura: Three Marcher armies held Segura, but the Jotun did not attack, and only minor skirmishes followed. The Lasambrian Jotun keep Anduzjasse and have made progress in Anozeseri.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: freeing Dark Ranging would open safer passage between Reikos and Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Imperial raiders crossed to Suaq Fount, sacked and collapsed the mithril mine at Ikka's Tears, freed two hundred thralls and mapped Jotun dispositions across the tundra.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: some raiders escaped Sermersuaq through the passes into Skarsind.
t.Spiral: The Grendel took Apstrus and Apulian, leaving only three regions in Imperial hands, so Spiral is no longer Imperial. Its remaining people huddle in their spires.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the spirits brewed at Bill Sabbey are popular as far afield as Tassato.
t.The Barrens: The Druj warbands aiding Brocéliande came from the armies camped in the Barrens. Striking them as they retreat could force those armies onto the defensive and inflict heavy casualties.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Keeper of the Breadbasket will spread its bounty across Upwold among other Marcher territories.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had retreated into Zenith after their earlier push into Spiral.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Thinly populated and far from the protective Night magic, Grey Fens fell swiftly to more than thirty thousand Jotun.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Sussivari's Night magic and the marsh beasts stalled the Bear-Who-Swims. Then thirty thousand more Jotun arrived, Greywater fell and the region was conquered.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The yeofolk of Ottery, Sallow and Graven Rock are making a defiant stand at Bill Sabbey. Heroes may defend it through the Sentinel Gate to rally the Marches.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Withering Winter magic was laid over the region, and five thousand Druj sworn to Arhallogen fought the vallorn here. Their retreat at the Gouged Oaks offers heroes a chance to strike.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The vallorn's exhaustion has left Dark Ranging exposed. A swift strike might free it and open a corridor along Brocéliande's western border.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The Valiant Pegasus and the Northern Eagle held Elerael against the climactic onslaught, though nearly a thousand soldiers were lost.
r.Brocéliande/Greenweald: Mentioned in passing: Druj scouts and guerrillas were seen as far east as the Greenweald.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: Terunael appears only in references to the fallen nation, the Scions of Terunael and the vallorn that devoured it.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Iron Gulls and Naguerro magicians are marching on Afar to stop its hakima's Night working. Heroes may intercept them through the Sentinel Gate.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Grendel marines secured the last of Fontargenta, and its fall carried the whole territory with it.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Imperial armies massed here, and the Granite Pillar drove off a Grendel assault on the newly built Mora's Rock. The Grendel now hold a fingerhold in the region.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Grendel ships landed two new armies here. Brief Imperial gains in the region were lost within weeks.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Druj scouts and saboteurs probed Ennerlund's mines but fell back when resisted. The lone survivor of a lost patrol was found near the Great Pits.
r.Holberg/Holfried: People living outside the walls took refuge in the upper city of Holfried as the garrison mobilised.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Residents of this district outside the walls abandoned their homes for the safety of Holfried.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Elite Druj arkad are closing on the Sand Fisher settlements in Misericorde. A Sentinel Gate conjunction could put heroes in their way.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Stealthy Druj scouts were reported in Rebeshof's marshes, threatening its farmers and herbalists.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The Druj are nearly three quarters of the way to claiming Utterlund, leaving the mutilated bodies of captured scouts along the forest edge.
r.Hordalant/Blutgahn: Mentioned in passing: Jotun champions raid out of the Blutgahn marshes into Grey Fens.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Winter Sun and the Green Shield marched through a mountain pass here, and the cheering garrison of Fort Braydon greeted them as relief.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Jotun withdrew before eleven thousand Imperial troops arrived, leaving only a Bear-Who-Swims banner and taking no thralls.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mentioned in passing: armies can only reach Kallavesa Marsh by going through Mitwold.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Mentioned in passing: armies can travel from West Marsh into North Fens.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Mentioned in passing: a new beachhead here is one way for Imperial armies to reach western Liathaven.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Mentioned in passing: a new beachhead here is one way for Imperial armies to reach western Liathaven.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: With Grey Fens in Jotun hands, Imperial armies cannot reach West Ranging without crossing Jotun land or first establishing a new beachhead.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: With Grey Fens in Jotun hands, Imperial armies cannot reach Westwood without crossing Jotun land or first establishing a new beachhead.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: The Lasambrian Jotun remained in Anduzjasse while Marcher armies planted their standards along its borders.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: The Jotun kept their hold on western Anozeseri's settlements and made some progress in conquering the contested region.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: A few minor, inconclusive skirmishes took place along the boundary of the Iron Plains.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Iron Qanat was raised in the Sobral Grasses, and caravans crossed the grasslands without interruption.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: A few minor, inconclusive skirmishes took place along the boundary of Yellow Chase.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The raiders landed here with hylje help and sank their boats. The Empire now has a strategic advantage in Suaq Fount, including no beachhead penalty for attacking it.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra remains in Imperial hands, and its people focus on defending their spires.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The Grendel conquered the thinly peopled region unopposed, overrunning or besieging its remaining spires.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Grendel forces took Apulian and set up a command post there, forcing Imperial troops back. The Druj also contest the region.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ateri remains in Imperial hands, and its people focus on defending their spires.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion remains in Imperial hands, and its people focus on defending their spires.
r.Spiral/Screed: Screed remains under Druj control. The Iron Gulls are survivors of the catastrophe that followed when its heart was roused.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: the Druj crossed into Holberg over the river from Farweald.

A broken frame.d: Three conjunctions targeted marshwalker threats in Holberg, Therunin and Kallavesa. In Ossium, the Druj miasma pillars at Red Lizard Point and the twin stones of Scorpion Glades could be broken, and a Druj and tortured-soul force at Korlack Marsh could be engaged. In Holberg, a Druj warband threatening the Legacy of Courage stelae and a Tepel apothecary's potion convoy could be struck. Rescue missions were offered for captured priests in Feroz, the Urizen engineer Minicia in Spiral and Grey Pilgrims in Segura and Therunin. Other conjunctions targeted vallorn incursions, a Jotun thrall camp, a Jotun blockade of the Gullet, mysterious Jotun lumbering in Liathaven, and sewer disappearances in Sarvos. These were opportunities, not outcomes.

n.Dawn: Dawnish priests and Day ritualists were called on to help break the Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, where consecration or the Chimes of Annulment could dispel the pall of dread.
n.Druj: Druj interests were targeted on several fronts: their miasma pillars in Ossium, the war party at Korlack Marsh, a warband destroying stelae in Holberg and a Tepel apothecary's escorted potion shipment in Utterlund.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held captive priests at the Fahran Wood Siegework near Mora and were taking the engineer Minicia south through Apstrus. Both offered the Empire chances to strike at their slave-taking.
n.Highguard: Highborn were drawn in by rescues of Grey Pilgrims held by Corazon orcs at Brejah Crag and trapped by vallorn in Greenheart. Highguard unconquered also reported husks threatening the Valiant Pegasus hospital, and Highborn soldiers were credited with protecting Feroz refugees.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs, alongside Wintermark, were invited to attack Varki's Camp so that Jotun thralls could escape into the wilds.
n.Jotun: Jotun positions faced Imperial attack at Varki's Camp in Sermersuaq and at their Cocklegullet base blockading the Gullet. Their unexplained mass felling of timber along Fallen Thorn Trail in Liathaven was also open to investigation.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were central to the vallorn and Heirs of Terunael threats in Brocéliande, Therunin and Hercynia, including a stranded band of trackers and a vate. They were also called to help against the marshlings in Therunin, to investigate Jotun lumbering in Liathaven, and were praised for protecting Feroz refugees.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn faced the aftermath of losing Feroz, with refugees fleeing inland and priests held by the Grendel near Mora. They were also concerned in the pilgrims' captivity in Segura, whose Corazon captors demanded 20 wains of mithril.
n.The League: The League faced threats to Holberg's mithril pumps from marshwalkers, to the Legacy of Courage stelae from a Druj warband, and to Druj supply lines in Utterlund. Its citizens were urged to explore the sewers of Sarvos for missing people.
n.The Marches: Marcher fleet-owners risked a one-rank profit penalty unless the Jotun base at Cocklegullet was removed. Marchers were also among those with an interest in the captive pilgrims in Segura.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the location of the pillar in Thule-held Bonewood was unknown, and it was unclear whether the mystics of Otkodov had already cleansed it.
n.Urizen: Urizen were offered a rescue mission for Minicia of the Illuminated Circle of Bloodsilver Twilight, the engineer behind the Block great work, before the Grendel could learn its secrets.
n.Varushka: Varushkan settlers in Ossium could see the miasma pillars broken and the Druj force plaguing Korlack Marsh destroyed, ending whispers that it might become the territory's first wolves. Varushka was also listed among those invited into the Sarvos sewers.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faced a marshwalker attack around Raimo's Fast in Kallavesa. It was also invited to raid Varki's Camp so that Jotun thralls could escape to Hahnmark or Kallavesa.

t.Bregasland: Jotun forces based outside Cocklegullet threatened to choke shipping on the Gullet, offering a conjunction to drive them out.
t.Brocéliande: A horde of vallorn husks, accompanied by suspected Heirs of Terunael, moved on the Valiant Pegasus field hospital at Swift Watch Woods in Elerael.
t.Feroz: With Feroz lost to the Grendel, refugees fled inland and captured priests were held at the Fahran Wood Siegework near Mora, awaiting possible rescue.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named as a possible refuge for Jotun thralls escaping Sermersuaq.
t.Hercynia: Navarr trackers and a vate were trapped by vallorn miasma and husks on the Bont Goch Trail, offering a chance to relieve them.
t.Holberg: Holberg faced a marshwalker threat to the Great Pits' mithril pumps, a Druj warband attacking the Legacy of Courage stelae, and a Druj potion convoy that could be ambushed.
t.Kallavesa: A marshwalker attacked the watchtowers around Raimo's Fast, injuring locals, though the Beacons network itself was not at risk.
t.Liathaven: Jotun warriors and thralls were felling timber on a massive scale along Fallen Thorn Trail for no clear purpose, and Navarr were invited to investigate.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Minicia's Grendel captors were thought possibly to be taking her to slave camps in Mareave.
t.Ossium: The Druj miasma pillars at Red Lizard Point and Scorpion Glades could be broken, and the Druj force terrorising the settlers of Korlack Marsh could be engaged.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the mystics of Otkodov might already have tried to cleanse the Bonewood pillar.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Reikos campaign was cited as the bitter lesson that clustered miasma pillars are harder to remove.
t.Sarvos: Disappearances and unease beneath the city, after a Winter curse and the arrival of the Iron Helms, prompted ten conjunctions into the unmapped sewers.
t.Segura: Highborn pilgrims preaching to Corazon orcs were held captive at Brejah Crag, and the Corazon demanded 20 wains of mithril for their return.
t.Sermersuaq: Many thralls had been moved to Varki's Camp, and an attack there could let large numbers escape Jotun rule.
t.Spiral: After the Grendel annexed Apstrus, the captured engineer Minicia was being taken south, and a rescue conjunction was offered.
t.Therunin: Marshlings threatened the Great Forest Orcs' Holt Outpost, and Grey Pilgrims were trapped by vallorn at Heart's Watch Steading.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: clashes in Zenith were cited as showing that clustered miasma pillars are harder to dispel.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Jotun base outside Cocklegullet on the Gullet's southern shore was targeted by a conjunction; if it was not removed, Marcher fleets would lose profits.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Vallorn husks and Heirs of Terunael threatened the Valiant Pegasus hospital at Swift Watch Woods, even though the vallorn's expansion into Elerael had already been stopped.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Mentioned in passing: refugees fleeing the Grendel were making for Afarjasse.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Captured priests were held at the Fahran Wood Siegework among the Grendel lines around Mora, and a rescue conjunction was offered.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: Navarr trackers and a vate were isolated in miasma on the Bont Goch Trail, surrounded by husks.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Converging marshwalker colonies threatened the South Wastes Drain pumps of the Great Pits, and a Druj warband stalked the Uitgang Road seeking more stelae to destroy.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The Druj presence there raised alarm, and a conjunction to the Barrens Trail offered a chance to ambush a Tepel apothecary's escorted potion shipment.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: A marshwalker destroyed structures and injured locals around Raimo's Fast, and those wounded needed aid.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: Jotun and thralls left felled timber strewn along miles of Fallen Thorn Trail, and Navarr could investigate why.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the location and status of the Bonewood pillar in Thule-held land were unknown.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Conjunctions offered the chance to break the pillar at Red Lizard Point and to fight the Druj and tortured souls plaguing the Korlack Marsh settlers.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Two miasma stones in the Scorpion Glades had to be depowered within about a minute of each other, amid tortured souls, to lift the dread.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: a pillar remained at Fang Tree, but no conjunction to it was detected.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Ten small conjunctions led into the unmapped Sewers of Sarvos to search for missing performers, a debutante, cadavers, a free company and lost ingots.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Highborn pilgrims were held by Corazon orcs at Brejah Crag, and a ransom of 20 wains of mithril was demanded.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: An attack on Varki's Camp could sow disruption among the Jotun and let many thralls escape before winter.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Minicia was being taken south through the Forest of Xanthi, and a rescue could be mounted there.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Grey Pilgrims left by the Heirs of Terunael at the ruins of Heart's Watch Steading held back advancing husks with a failing ward.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Marshlings emerging from the swamps advanced on Holt Outpost, the Great Forest Orcs' watchpost guarding the Holt of the Oak.

A mountain of vipers.d: After the Axou rejected slavery and Maximillian Ankarien's mandate urged trade, the new Grand Ilarch Andronicus opened Issyk's port and invited the Empire to build Imperial docks there for 30 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns. Issyk and Maykop traders added streams to the Quaymaster of the Black Sails and the Eastern Broker. The Purple Sails and the Sarvos and Tassato Chambers of Commerce asked the Synod whether selling liao to Axos was acceptable, and two competing mandates were proposed. Hesychia of Elos proposed the Elosian Docks in Redoubt to trade dragonbone for white granite. Maykop offered a student exchange and ilium through a proposed House of Spirits. All offers would lapse after Winter Solstice 383YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Astolat and Semmerholm are listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the proposed House of Spirits could be built.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Tanwyn Ankarien is recalled as having led Imperial mercenaries to help Ipotavo fight off a Druj invasion.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Issyk's former alliance with the orcs of the Broken Shore is recalled, and the new Grand Ilarch is critical of Issyk's dealings with the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is a candidate site for the House of Spirits, and the Litharge in Necropolis is named as a place Axou students might attend.
n.Navarr: If the Eastern Broker's offices survive the vallorn, the Navarr title would gain a third stream to buy cerulean mazzarine, ambergelt and green iron from Issyk. A Navarr scholar's account of Maykop is cited, and Miaren is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Fellowship of Purple Sails helped put the question of the liao trade to the Synod, hoping to profit from Axou demand. Madruga is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.
n.The League: League merchants were central to the push: the Chambers of Commerce of Sarvos and Tassato put the liao question to the Synod, and Issyk sent ships to Sarvos. Four League cities are candidate sites for the House of Spirits, and the University of Holberg might receive Axou students.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizen Hesychia of Elos proposed refitting the docks at Elos in Redoubt to trade dragonbone for Axou white granite. Urizen's places of learning would also welcome Axou students if the Senate opened its universities to them.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Karov is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Holberg: Holberg is a candidate site for the House of Spirits, and its University is named among the institutions Axou students would seek to join if the Senate opened its universities to them.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the prestigious Litharge in Necropolis is named among the places Axou students would seek to attend if the student exchange went ahead.
t.Redoubt: Hesychia of Elos proposed refitting the old docks at Elos to welcome Axou traders, exchanging dragonbone for white granite. The work would need a Senate motion and commission, 30 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns, and would create a Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks title.
t.Sarvos: Issyk sent ships to Sarvos announcing that its port was open to Imperial trade. The Sarvos Chamber of Commerce joined the delegation asking the Synod to rule on the liao trade, and Sarvos is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Tassato: The Tassato Chamber of Commerce helped bring the liao question to the Synod, prompted by merchants such as Mariana di Tassato. The city is also a candidate site for the House of Spirits.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: the Litharge of Necropolis is named as a likely destination for Axou students; no specific location within the territory is given.

A pleasing and deceptive face.d: Eleonaris refused a parley but invited named courtiers to meet her diplomats in the Hall of Fellowship. Surut offered parley to the Winter Archmage and asked to meet several named groups. Estavus proposed a veilingmarkt auction of goods and enchantments for materials. Lashonar opened the Caucus Forum to the Archmage of Night and the Imperial Consul. Kimus agreed to parley with the Archmage of Day, the Imperial Seer, Spymaster and Penumbral Watcher, but rejected a general meeting on magic. A briar emissary told Navarr vates at the Broch that Yaw'nagrah would grant no audience. A Jarmish magician delivered Ter Andzrev's request; the Imperial Archivist found the name may belong to Ossegrahn, an eternal once declared an enemy by the Conclave.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, was refused a parley by Yaw'nagrah, told the favour shown to last year's Dawnish archmage would not be repeated, and was asked by "Lord Rain" to attend a formal parley; Urien Novarion of Dawn was also invited to meet Eleonaris's diplomats.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Yaw'nagrah's briar emissary accused the Navarr of preferring to embrace the Druj over the gifts of the Green Mother.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the page closes with a quotation on the deceptive faces of eternals from Saul of Cantiarch's Hold, a Highborn magister writing in 27YE.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Gralka of the Imperial Orcs, Archmage of Day, was invited by Kimus to bring the Imperial Seer, Spymaster and Penumbral Watcher to meet two senior heralds, though her request for a general meeting on magic was refused.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates and thorns at the Broch received and passed on Yaw'nagrah's hostile message, then turned their backs on the briar emissary mid-speech; separately, Syn Truth-Walker Returned of Navarr, Archmage of Winter, was offered a midnight parley with Surut.
n.Urizen: Two Urizen archmages received answers: Edmundo of Damakan's Forge, Archmage of Autumn, was offered Estavus's veilingmarkt and talks on construct use, and Elyssiathain, Archmage of Night, was granted entry to Lashonar's Caucus Forum.

t.Brocéliande: A briar emissary of Yaw'nagrah, flanked by two towering tree-creatures, delivered the Green Mother's refusal of parley at the Broch amid the Navarr's muted celebration of the vallorn's defeat, before withdrawing into the trees without violence.

All the news from Twin Town.d: Merchant-Prince Benjamin of the Featherwick Guild proposed refurbishing his great aunt's derelict building in Regario as an Imperial Consulate, requiring a Senate motion, weirwood, white granite and 80 crowns. He also suggested the Consul appoint ambassadors, an option later withdrawn. After Alfredo Barossa's statement inviting Seren to become the fifth League city, Tassatans proposed markets at Tagliano and Holt, and a Mestran Hills Mutual Association trading ore for Navarr herbs. Merchant-Prince Mariana von Mestra drafted a Synod mandate offering the Whittle folk sanctuary in Little Mournwold, at the cost of their green iron. Rumours of murder, sabotage or rioting surrounded the Arratan Gamble quarries.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are said to have preferred dealing with the Imperial Fleet Master over the Consul, and Prince Benjamin does not count the Fleet Master as a proper ambassador whatever they say.
n.Highguard: Gossips claimed the incident at the Arratan Gamble quarries was the work of a secret society seeking to remove the Highborn holder of the seat, Ames of Reikos.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun advance is recalled as having driven the Whittle villagers from their homes to Tassato in 380YE.
n.Navarr: The League statement inviting Seren to join it got a mixed reception among the Navarr. In response, Tassatans proposed joint markets at Tagliano and Holt and a trading association giving Navarr herb garden owners their own Imperial title overseeing a metal ministry.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities that could only join the League if Madruga seceded, something pundits called inconceivable.
n.The League: Tassato offered several proposals: an Imperial Consulate, trade works with Navarr, a League Bourse title overseeing a herb ministry, and a possible Synod mandate granting the Whittle folk sanctuary. Sarvos, Holberg and Temeschwar remained preoccupied with curses and attacks.
n.The Marches: The Little Mournwold enclave of Marchers in Tassato Mestra is troubled by the Marcher assembly's ultimatum to the Whittle folk. A proposed League mandate would offer the Whittle folk sanctuary away from orcs.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are noted as preferring to deal with the Varushkans rather than the Consul, even after agreeing to embassies between Otkodov and the Empire.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among cities that could not join the League without Hahnmark seceding, and the Feni are said to have ignored the Consul during trouble in Hahnmark.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: some Marchers settled in Little Mournwold in Tassato come from as far afield as Bregasland.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is cited as a territory that would have to secede for Kalpaheim to join the League, and as a scene of recent unpleasantness involving the Feni.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's people are described as dealing with curses that withered their gardens.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named as a territory that would need to secede for Siroc to join the League, which was deemed inconceivable.
t.Miaren: Miaren could gain a market at Holt as part of the proposed Road to Seren, giving its forest owners a seasonal share of 54 crowns. Its herbalists could also trade with Tassatan miners through the proposed Mutual Association.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as a territory that would need to secede for Meade to join the League.
t.Mournwold: The Whittle folk of the Mournwold faced the Marcher assembly's ultimatum. A proposed League mandate would let many of them leave for sanctuary in Tassato, ending the green iron from the Whittle Hill mine.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as the site of grudgingly agreed embassies between the Thule and the Empire.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Arratan Gamble seat is held by Ames of Reikos, whom rumour named as the target of the quarry incident.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's people are described as dealing with curses that shattered their mirrors.
t.Tassato: Tassato enjoyed relative peace and became the source of proposals for an Imperial Consulate, trade works with Seren, and sanctuary for the Whittle folk. Meanwhile rumours of trouble swirled around its Arratan Gamble quarries.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's people are preparing for further attacks, and the city is cited as a historical example of a city joining the League.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: some Marchers settled in Little Mournwold in Tassato come from Upwold.

r.Miaren/Holtford: The town of Holt was proposed as the Navarr half of the Road to Seren markets, with warehouses to channel lumber trade towards Tassato.
r.Tassato/Enterio: A week before the Autumn Equinox, rumours spread of an incident at the Arratan Gamble's white granite quarries, with talk of murder, sabotage and rioting likely exaggerated.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: Gemma Stewart's Forge and Furnace Fellowship proposed building a trading post at the base of the hills in western Madeiras, where mining guilds would sell ore to the Navarr in exchange for herbs.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Little Mournwold in Mestra hosts a thriving Marcher enclave and could take in returning Whittle folk under a proposed mandate. They might then help revive the old mine workings above the city.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: A derelict four-storey building near the University of Tassato in Regario, with its own dock, was proposed for refurbishment as the Imperial Consulate.

Appraise Sign of Tamar.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion directed Graciana i Lopez i Guerra to carry out the appraisal. It asked two questions: how the Sign of Tamar could be kept from being swallowed by the encroaching forest, and what uses the Empire could make of it once it was preserved. The motion passed, and the appraisal was due to be delivered before the Winter Solstice. The motion itself committed no work or resources to preserving the site. It only commissioned the study.

n.Highguard: Highguard held Reikos at the time, so this appraisal concerned a site within Highborn-held land whose preservation and future use the Senate had chosen to investigate.

t.Reikos: The Senate commissioned a study into preserving the Sign of Tamar in Reikos from the forest and making use of it for the Empire, with the report due before the Winter Solstice.

r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode is home to the Sign of Tamar, which faced being reclaimed by the forest. The appraisal was commissioned to find ways to save it and put it to Imperial use.

Construct Blackfield Market.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, the motion sought to disburse Senate funds to construct the Blackfield Market in Mitwold. It would have created the title of Blackfield Bailiff, appointed annually through the Imperial Bourse by a vote of the farm owners of the Marches, to oversee the market. The motion was framed as taking advantage of a recent proposal to construct a ministry for purchasing white granite. It failed, so the market was not commissioned and the Bailiff title was not created.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators for Bregasland and Mitwold put forward a market and a Bailiff title to be chosen by the nation's farm owners, but the motion failed and the Marches gained neither.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold was the proposed site of the Blackfield Market, but the motion to fund its construction failed, so nothing was built there.

Construct Defence of the Broch.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Therunin, the motion passed at 150 thrones. It took advantage of an opportunity offered by the people of the steadings and was subject to non-standard costs: 40 wains of weirwood, 80 crowns in labour and three months of construction. Merlin Feyerd provided over nine thrones and 14 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox, alongside small donations. Llewellyn Leafstalker added 10 wains after the Winter Solstice and 16 more after the Spring Equinox 384YE. The completed works were to protect the Broch, give a bounty of 75 bladeroot to every personal resource in Brocéliande except military units and fleets, and serve as a spy network in the territory.

t.Brocéliande: Although the Vallorn held Brocéliande at the time, the Defence of the Broch was to guard the Broch there, provide 75 bladeroot to each personal resource in the territory and give the Empire a spy network within it.

Construct Forest of Defiance.d: Palerictrus Krunk, describing himself as Bearer of an Imperial Orc Wayleave, announced the Forest of Defiance. It is a mana sinecure costing 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Its title, Dauntless Warrior, is to be appointed for life by all Imperial Orc senators and can be revoked by the Imperial Orc national assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine. After the Autumn Equinox, Krunk supplied the 10 wains of mithril, Tog gave 2 thrones 3 crowns 19 rings, and small donations added 1 ring. The Speaker's note records that the Wayleave title was vacant when the announcement was made, and the matter is being investigated.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs stand to gain a mana sinecure whose Dauntless Warrior title would be appointed by their senators and could be revoked by their national assembly. The commission was, however, announced under an Imperial Orc Wayleave title that was vacant at the time, and that is now under investigation.

t.Skarsind: The Forest of Defiance mana sinecure is to be constructed in Skarsind. Its mithril and some of its labour costs had been provided after the Autumn Equinox 383YE.

Construct Good Walder's Orchard.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Bregasland. It was intended to be entirely self-funded by Bastard Tom of Upwold, with the stated aim of raising an inspirational tomb there in future. The sinecure creates the one-year position of Keeper of the Orchard, appointed and revocable by the Marcher Assembly. Non-standard costs applied: 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour. After the Autumn Equinox, Tom Appleseed provided 7 thrones 2 crowns and the 30 wains of white granite, and Lieselotte van Holberg provided a further 2 crowns.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a sinecure, Good Walder's Orchard, that yields apples and liao each season. The Marcher Assembly controls its Keeper of the Orchard, appointing the holder for a year and able to revoke the title.

t.Mitwold: The orchard was commissioned by the Walder's Oak in Mitwold, with a future inspirational tomb intended at the site.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator proposed the motion, and it was to be funded by Bastard Tom of Upwold.

Construct House Bourné School of Couture.d: Proposed by the Senator for Sarvos and seconded by Weirwater, the motion drew on an opportunity presented by House Bourné. It was to be funded by the Looking Glass and prosperous Sarvos citizens with help from the Highborn Benefactors, at a non-standard cost of 6 wains of weirwood, 6 wains of white granite and 45 thrones. Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos provided almost all of it (44 thrones 7 crowns plus all the materials), with Lieselotte van Holberg giving the final crown. The Senator confirmed the Mirrored Maschieri would be a Senate appointment, championing fashion and design across the Empire while a vice-chancellor runs the school day to day.

n.The League: League senators for Sarvos and Weirwater proposed and seconded the folly, and League citizens almost entirely funded it, giving the nation a new Imperial institution of couture and a Senate-appointed champion of fashion.

t.Sarvos: The House Bourné School of Couture is to be built in Sarvos, paid for by its prosperous citizens, offering the chance to rebuild the city as the City of Masks.

Construct Iron Roads.d: The motion passed at 100 thrones, with non-standard costs of 200 wains of white granite and 400 crowns of labour, one year of construction and one Senate commission. Between Autumn 383YE and Winter 384YE, Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied most of the granite and money, with further contributions from Lieselotte van Holberg, Tomasz, Vesna Borkovna Prochnost and Borz nikoli strazkovitch. Once complete, the roads would act as a great work in Miekarova, Karov and Volodmartz. They would also add 2 wains a season to the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the Night Quarry while the roads stayed open. Completing them might open further industrial opportunities across the north-east.

n.The League: If the roadbuilding projects were completed, more Varushkan materials could flow to Temeschwar, possibly giving the League an opportunity to expand the Assayer's Guild.
n.Varushka: Varushka gains a major road network linking isolated vales. The roads promise a great work in three of its territories, better output from several Bourse resources, and possible future investment in its industrial might, largely funded by Varushkans such as Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov.

t.Karov: Once completed, the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in Karov.
t.Karsk: Completing the grand roadbuilding projects could bring easier access to the mines of Karsk as a future opportunity.
t.Miekarova: The senator for Miekarova seconded the motion, and once completed the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in the territory.
t.Temeschwar: The completed roads might send more materials flowing to Temeschwar, offering a possible opportunity to expand the Assayer's Guild there.
t.Volodmartz: Once completed, the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in Volodmartz.

Construct Lepidean University.d: Proposed by Bastion's senator and seconded by Casinea's, the commission cost 60 wains of white granite, 30 wains of weirwood and 180 crowns in labour, with 20 thrones upkeep, and took six months. The materials were supplied by Rhesa, Asael and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, with private donors giving over 22 thrones. The Lepidean Librarian, appointed by the Highborn National Assembly, may conduct historical research into paragons, exemplars or true liao visions. The Constitutional Court debated the use of the judgement of rewarding for the true liao at length but allowed it on historical precedent, and amended the guidance so that competing judgements are decided by the greatest margin of votes.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a university and the Lepidean Librarian, a title appointed and revocable by its National Assembly, with powers to research paragons, exemplars and true liao visions; Highborn citizens Rhesa and Asael supplied much of the granite and weirwood.

t.Bastion: The Lepidean University was commissioned in Bastion, with its senator proposing the motion that would bring the university and a dose of true liao to the territory.

Construct Pegasus Respite.d: The Pegasus Respite was commissioned as a sinecure at a cost of 14 wains of weirwood and 28 crowns in labour, taking three months to build, and was announced as fully self-funded. Its herbs were intended for Highguard's battle physicks in service of the Empire. The House of the Proffered Hand was to run a former slave rehabilitation wing on the premises to support the convalescent hospital's work. Funding came mainly from Tolame, who provided 3 thrones and 12 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 383YE and a further 2 crowns 19 rings and 2 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Septus Sentinels Tower and small donors added smaller sums. Once completed, the commission would be overseen by the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite.

n.Highguard: The Highborn national assembly gained the right to appoint the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite, and the herbs it produced were destined for Highguard's battle physicks.

t.Reikos: Reikos, held by Highguard, became the site of a new convalescent sinecure, which included a rehabilitation wing for former slaves run by the House of the Proffered Hand.

r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Chalcis Mount was chosen as the location of the Pegasus Respite, a convalescent hospital and herb-producing sinecure built over three months.

Construct Skarsind College of Pitfightin.d: The commission required 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour costs and three months to build, on top of the standard costs. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Palerictus Dura provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 5 wains of white granite, and Bloodcrow Yargol provided the other 5 wains of white granite. Once it is complete, the College will be overseen by a new Imperial title, the Pitmaster.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gain a pitfighting college in their homeland of Skarsind, with a new Pitmaster title to oversee it. One of the two contributors of white granite was Bloodcrow Yargol.

t.Skarsind: The College of Pitfighting is being built at Skogi in Skarsind. Once it is finished, the territory will be home to a business sinecure overseen by the Pitmaster.

Construct Trees and Hills merchant hall.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Ossium, the motion commissioned a ministry in Karsk to help Ossium's refugees settle and to exchange forest or mine resources for coin. It created the title Warden of the Trees and Hills, elected once a year by the forest and mine owners of Varushka. The commission required 6 wains of white granite, 6 wains of mithril and 24 crowns of labour. After the Autumn Equinox, Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov provided the mithril, the white granite and 3 thrones. Work could not begin, however, because the location of the Warden's offices had not been decided.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new elected title, the Warden of the Trees and Hills, chosen each year by the nation's forest and mine owners. Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied the materials for the hall.

t.Karsk: Karsk's senator proposed the motion to build the merchant hall in Karsk, which would organise Ossium refugees settling there. Work cannot start until the Warden's office location is decided.
t.Ossium: Ossium's senator seconded the motion, which sought to organise Ossium's displaced people as they settle in neighbouring Karsk.

Construct spy network in Skallahn.d: Cayleb of Felix's Watch used his authority as Imperial Spymaster to announce the commission of a spy network in the Jotun-held territory of Skallahn. The commission required 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns, plus an upkeep of 2 thrones. After the Autumn Equinox, Cayleb himself provided 2 thrones 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood towards it. The page does not record the network as finished; once complete, Imperial military units would be able to support the spy network.

n.Jotun: The Empire moved to plant a network of spies in the Jotun territory of Skallahn, extending Imperial intelligence-gathering into Jotun lands.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is located as lying west of Sermersuaq and Kallavesa, both Wintermark territories at the time.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: used as a reference point, with Skallahn described as lying to its west.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: used as a reference point, with Skallahn described as lying to its west.
t.Skallahn: An Imperial spy network was commissioned in this Jotun-held territory, with weirwood and money supplied towards it; once complete, Imperial military units would be able to support it.

Crowned in rose and heather.d: No egregore can sense either missing figure, so the Court ruled both titles vacant, a decision that stands even if they return. Rival memorials were proposed: a park and pavilion in Holberg, or a Custodes Clavium granite tower in the Necropolis. The Senate might make the Chamberlain an Imperial title and decide the future of the Imperial Offices. The Synod could name her greatest achievement, endorse pilgrimage mandates inspired by her final address, or recognise possible ascension or a miracle in the Frieze of Flowers, whose depiction of her now appears to change. The Court also tightened its guidance so that using her Imperial favour in the Senate or Military Council consumes it.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: patriotic volunteers from Dawn and Holberg would provide the labour for the proposed memorial park in Holberg.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis is the traditional resting place of Thrones, and the Custodes Clavium offered to design a white granite tower there as her memorial. Her final address also fed interest in pilgrimage already strong among the Grey Pilgrims.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Imperatrix was credited with fortifying the Mourn after the rout of the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the page notes the appeal of encouraging pilgrims to walk the trods as the Navarr do.
n.The League: The League lost its Empress, Lisabetta von Holberg, whom its egregore can no longer sense. Many League citizens want her memorialised at home, and League figures such as Severin Teyhard von Holberg, Ortenzia di Sarvos and Benedict Pacelli von Holberg were tied to her offices or proposed mandates.
n.The Marches: Many common Marchers saw the Throne as their last defence against the Military Council, and they now fear for the interdiction of curses such as Rivers Run Red.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost a staunch supporter of its military, and the page asks who will now champion its cause while it is threatened on two fronts.
n.Varushka: Varushka's egregore can no longer sense Imperial Magus Juha, and unconfirmed reports say the Varushkan magician Simargl, the Empty One, guided the pair on a quest into the Dreamscape.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kellua Itsepainen of Wintermark was one of the Imperatrix's senior chamberlains, and the vanished Empress Mariika is cited as a precedent.

t.Bastion: Pilgrims to Bastion customarily visit the Necropolis, which many argue is the right place for the Imperatrix's official memorial.
t.Bay of Catazar: Doubts arose over whether the great plan to fortify the territories around the Bay of Catazar can be completed without an Empress to pay for it.
t.Holberg: Holberg was the Empress's home city, and architect Katarzyna von Carstein proposed a memorial park and white stone pavilion there. It would need a Senate commission, 50 wains of weirwood and 25 of white granite.
t.Mournwold: The Imperatrix was unexpectedly popular in the Mournwold, credited with its development and fortification, and her loss raised the greatest concern here, including over the interdiction of Rivers Run Red.
t.Necropolis: Tradition places Thrones' tombs here, and the Custodes Clavium offered a 189-step tower of 50 wains of white granite. Building it would need a Senate motion and 100 crowns but would not use a civil service commission slot.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Empress Mariika walking into Sydanjaa in 234YE is cited as an earlier Throne who disappeared without trace.

Desolation of Yoorn.d: The curse lasts around thirty years, steadily reducing births and harvests while leaving the vallorn slothful unless provoked. Liathaven Navarr may move free to Hercynia, Miaren or Therunin. The Jotun are likely to evacuate their thralls, and hungry Feni may raid neighbouring lands. Tharim and Surut offered to take Liathaven if the Senate ceded it, turning it into a cursed wasteland hostile to armies until about 413YE. Heeding Corey Wayfarer's assembly statement, Brocéliande's people will stay until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE, then leave if the curse remains. Lifting it would need a vast Spring working, and a proposed Navarr mandate could reveal ways to do it.

n.Jotun: The Jotun will likely see the curse as an attack on their thralls and evacuate them from Liathaven, though warriors seeking glory may stay. A Court-blighted Liathaven would make it far harder for their armies to reach the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Navarr families in Liathaven and Brocéliande face a choice between their homes and their descendants' future. Their assembly urged them to stay, and a proposed mandate could rally the nation to find magic to lift the curse from Brocéliande.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the civil service suggest that famished Feni might even raid as far as Kahraman.
n.The Marches: Marcher lands in the southern Mournwold and Bregasland face anticipated Feni raids as the curse starves the forest folk. A blighted Liathaven would also deter Jotun armies from reaching the Mournwold.

t.Bregasland: The civil service anticipate Feni raids into Bregasland as the curse leaves the Feni short of food.
t.Brocéliande: The territory now lies under Wither the Seed. Its people will stay until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE to give Dark Ranging a chance to be freed, but a steady exodus will begin if the curse is not lifted.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia is one of the territories Liathaven Navarr may move to without the usual fee, keeping their resource upgrades if they move before the end of the Winter Solstice 383YE.
t.Liathaven: The already depopulated territory is cursed for some thirty years and would remain a drain on the treasury even if reconquered. The Thrice-cursed Court have offered to take it and turn it into a cursed wasteland if the Senate cedes it.
t.Miaren: Miaren, freed from the vallorn under Emperor Giovanni using this same curse, is now a fee-free destination for Navarr leaving Liathaven.
t.Mournwold: The southern Mournwold may suffer Feni raids, while a Court-blighted Liathaven would make it much harder for Jotun armies to reach the Mournwold.
t.Therunin: Therunin is one of the territories Liathaven Navarr may move to without the usual fee, with help to keep their resource upgrades if they move before the end of the Winter Solstice 383YE.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Mentioned in passing: Boar's Dell is named as one of the two regions where most of Brocéliande's Navarr live under the curse.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The chance to free Dark Ranging from the vallorn is why Brocéliande's people will endure the curse until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Mentioned in passing: Elerael is named alongside Boar's Dell as home to most of Brocéliande's Navarr.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, appearing only as part of cursed Brocéliande and through references to the Heirs of Terunael.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: West Ranging would be among the first regions given to the Thrice-cursed Court if ceded. The Court would allow the Empire to harvest its newly found weirwood grove, but at significantly higher cost.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Westwood is one of the two regions where the Thrice-cursed Court's malicious influence would initially be confined if the Senate cedes them.

Disbursement of funds for College of Eng.d: Proposed by the Senator for Tassato and seconded by the Senator for Redoubt, the motion sought a disbursal of funds to finish building the Adamant College in Temeschwar. It followed a previous motion to disburse funds for the College of Engineering and Architecture. The motion passed at 120 thrones, and that sum was disbursed to the Senator for Tassato to complete the work.

n.The League: League senators for Tassato and Redoubt jointly secured 120 thrones from the Imperial treasury to finish the Adamant College on League soil.

t.Temeschwar: The 120 thrones were granted to complete construction of the Adamant College in Temeschwar, the territory's College of Engineering and Architecture.

Double dare.d: Donations from Freeborn citizens gave every military unit supporting the armies in Segura an extra 5 Crowns. Because those armies stayed on defence, the bounty would continue only for units supporting armies that attack in Segura. With Feroz fallen to the Grendel, a proposed mandate needing a greater majority would extend the bounty to armies attacking there, at the cost of a one-rank production penalty to all other Brass Coast personal resources. Conflicting judgements on privateering caused confusion, but corsairs found four targets: the Temple of Tempest Jade, the Vorlach slave markets, Asavean granite ships and the Drake Island shipyard. Full plans for the chosen raid were promised before the Winter Solstice.

n.Grendel: Having taken Feroz, the Grendel faced a possible bounty on armies attacking them there and proposed corsair raids on their temple, their slave markets at Vorlach, their Asavean granite trade or the four warship hulls at their Drake Island shipyard.
n.Jotun: The Jotun did not attack the defended armies in Segura, and the Freeborn would now fund the bounty only for armies that attack Jotun forces there.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn citizens paid for the defence of Segura and could choose to pay again for Feroz, at the cost of lost production. Their corsair families awaited the Assembly's choice of a single raid against the Grendel.

t.Bay of Catazar: Corsair ships scoured the Bay for opportunities. Asavean merchantmen carrying slaves and white granite sail through it unescorted, making them a possible but illegal target unless the Senate declared war on the Asaveans.
t.Feroz: Feroz fell to the Grendel, and a proposed mandate would extend the Freeborn Bounty to military units supporting armies that attack the invaders there.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: any Grendel warships captured in a raid on Drake Island might be sailed back to Madruga.
t.Segura: Units supporting the armies in Segura received an extra 5 Crowns, but no fighting took place. The bounty would continue only for armies that undertake attacking orders against the Jotun there.
t.Shayeel: The mining and slave-market town of Vorlach on Shayeel's northern coast, controlled by Salt Lord Moorvain, was a possible raid target. Such a raid would need Imperial military units as well as fleets, and could free many slaves and carry off mithril.

Expand the Kruidenkenner Magazjin.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Madruga, the motion took up the Kruidenkenner guild of herbalists' opportunity, available for the last season. It created no new titles but enhanced the ministries of the High Herbalist of Sybella, the Master of the Clearing House, the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel and the Kruidenkenner Trademaster. The civilian commission cost 24 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns in labour and took three months. Dino i Riqueza provided 6 thrones and the 24 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the High Herbalist, the Master of the Clearing House and the Trademaster gained a ministry for buying Sarcophan herbs. The Vizier also gained one, but the Senate must first establish new offices as described in the To curb those raging appetites Wind of Fortune.

n.Highguard: Highguard's High Herbalist of Sybella saw their ministry significantly enhanced, gaining access to herbs bought from the Sarcophans through the expanded Magazjin in Highguard's own territory of Necropolis.
