t.Necropolis: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay in Necropolis was expanded and completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 383YE, becoming the base for an Imperial herb trade with the Sarcophans.

Fall of Brocéliande.d: The vallorn's expansion was stymied and Winter magic hinders its recovery. Clearing Dark Ranging would require Imperial armies to claim the entire region, with casualties doubled by the miasma and supporting military units suffering lasting losses. Dawnish rewards and Highborn pilgrim aid continued until the Winter Solstice, with Highguard able to recall or extend its pilgrims by mandate. Tharim offered continued and potentially greater aid at the cost of more herb gardens and forests. The Great Forest Orcs went home, disgusted by Druj aid to the Navarr. Proposals were made to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing in Elerael, the last conditional on a Navarr statement condemning the Druj alliance. It was later withdrawn.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units supporting armies in Brocéliande continued to earn four random ingots from the nobles of Rucastle and Semmerholm until the Winter Solstice. Rucastle also proposed fortifying Greenstead as a castle for questing knights.
n.Druj: Druj aid to the Navarr in northern Brocéliande drove the Great Forest Orcs home and angered Highborn pilgrims, and the Broch scouting was meant to check for Druj surprises left in Boar's Dell.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations kept losing Synod votes and liao while their pilgrims aided Brocéliande, worth about 1,400 strength to any attack. The national assembly could recall them early or extend their service by mandate, and a Highborn physick co-proposed the Houses of Healing.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Liathaven's earlier weakened vallorn was cited as a comparison, and its curse was covered elsewhere.
n.Navarr: The Navarr of Brocéliande survived the vallorn surge and were offered a chance to reclaim Dark Ranging, along with proposals to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing. The healing houses depended on the national assembly condemning the Druj alliance.
n.Wintermark: Tharim offered to triple his aid in Brocéliande if the Conclave let him feed on the herb gardens and forests of Wintermark and other nations, each losing two herbs or resources until Winter 384YE.

t.Brocéliande: The weakened vallorn could be driven from Dark Ranging before it recovered by Autumn 384YE. Proposals to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing in Elerael were put forward to strengthen the territory.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: a fortification at the Broch, if Black Boughs were cleared, would help guard the eastern approach to Casinea.
t.Hercynia: Herb gardens and forests in Hercynia continued to lose two herbs or two measures each to Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: its previously weakened vallorn was used as a comparison, and the Winter curse over it was covered in another Wind of Fortune.
t.Miaren: Herb gardens and forests in Miaren continued to lose two herbs or two measures each to Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: clearing Dark Ranging would let armies move from Reikos to Semmerholm or the Barrens, and the fall of Reikos was recalled.
t.Semmerholm: The nobles of Rucastle and Semmerholm continued rewarding Dawnish units in Brocéliande, and clearing Dark Ranging would open an army route between Semmerholm and Reikos.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: clearing Dark Ranging would let armies pass from Reikos into the Barrens, and Greenstead serves knights exploring there.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orc warriors returned to Therunin in disgust at Druj aid, and its herb gardens and forests kept suffering Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Mentioned in passing: if the vallorn were driven from Black Boughs, the Broch would be an ideal site for a fortification.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell withstood the vallorn surge, and Rucastle proposed fortifying its steading of Greenstead as a Dawnish-style castle and base for questing into the vallorn.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Imperial armies could clear the vallorn from Dark Ranging, but only by claiming the whole region before Autumn 384YE, fighting in miasma that doubles casualties.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael held against the vallorn with Highborn and Great Forest Orc help, and Houses of Healing were proposed at Eleri's Stead, conditional on the Navarr condemning the Druj alliance.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not discussed, though the Heirs of Terunael are named as a threat the Broch could watch for.

Great prosperity and strength.d: With the Cinderpath Exchange built, white granite withheld by virtuous citizens went to auction (about a dozen extra wains) and to the Cinderpath Custodian. Ilium meant for the lost Broken Shore Bounty went partly to auction and partly, as a private gift, to Imperial Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra. The Iron Roundtower was built, while the Invisible Cord Brokerage was commissioned but not yet built. The Marches were offered the Blackfield Market. Dawn, the Imperial Orcs, Wintermark, Urizen and the League received outline proposals, each needing a statement of principle with a greater majority. Bishop Imago Monta also suggested an Ombudsman of the Bourse. Wintermark backed Valashal, Dawn failed to back Applefell, and interest faded by Winter.

n.Dawn: Dawnish yeofolk proposed a weirwood market-faire at Applefell and an ilium Star Metal Market at Lacre, both overseen by yeofolk appointed by military unit captains. The Dawnish assembly failed to win a greater majority for Applefell.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Legacy mine remains in Druj hands, and the loss of Zenith is cited as a blow to Urizen.
n.Grendel: The Grendel invasion of Feroz cost the Empire the Scorrero Nets and the Broken Shore Bounty, leaving Bay of Catazar ilium undeliverable to its Freeborn seat.
n.Highguard: The Cinderpath Exchange was finally built in Highguard. Highborn who had withheld white granite at the Synod's urging now offered it to the Cinderpath Custodian, and other withheld granite went to auction.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orcs were offered a possible Miner's Market at Krysse in Skarsind, where a bonesetter appointed by military unit owners could buy mithril at reasonable prices, if their assembly showed interest with a greater majority.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Pride of Ikka's Tears now serves the Jotun once repaired, and a new weirwood grove has been found in Jotun-held Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Invisible Cord Brokerage was commissioned in Navarr but not yet built. If completed, it is expected to reduce the weirwood available at the public auction.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost the Broken Shore Bounty and Scorrero Nets. Grateful mariners began gifting ilium to Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, and the Freeborn are discussing the mithril-dealing Parador of Dust.
n.The League: League merchant-princes proposed a single market in Holberg, Tassato, Temeschwar or Sarvos buying all four Bourse resources. It would need an assembly statement choosing the city, and how it would be appointed remained hotly debated.
n.The Marches: Following its assembly's call for an exchange, the Marches were offered the Blackfield Market in Mitwold. It would buy white granite under a Blackfield Bailiff elected annually by Marcher farm owners.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule invasion and conquest of Skarsind is recalled as the cause of Gulhule's and Krysse's past losses.
n.Urizen: Urizeni architects proposed a market in northern Siluri in Redoubt for mithril, ilium or both, which would need an assembly statement naming the resources. This came after Urizen's prosperity suffered from losing Zenith, the invasion of Morrow and fighting over Spiral.
n.Varushka: The Varushkans completed the Iron Roundtower, reducing mithril at the public auction. Its title became available for appointment at the Autumn Equinox.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark traders proposed Gulnar's Deephall for mithril and a Valashal hall for white granite, with each also able to buy some ilium. The Wintermark assembly indicated that Valashal would benefit the nation.

t.Bay of Catazar: Fisherfolk and mariners unable to deliver ilium to the Broken Shore Bounty sent 10 rings to auction (then about four a season). Wealthier captains sent six rings to the Fleet Master, then four a season, with help from the Fellowship of the Purple Sails.
t.Casinea: An estimated additional dozen wains of white granite, released by citizens who had withheld it, were brought to Casinea to be auctioned.
t.Feroz: The Grendel invasion of Feroz cost the Empire the offices of the Broken Shore Bounty and the Scorrero Nets.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's merchants and miners proposed two possible trading halls: Gulnar's Deephall for mithril and a hall at Valashal for white granite, each also buying some ilium.
t.Holberg: Holberg was one of four League cities that could host the proposed market buying all four Bourse resources.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to ilium netted along Varushkan shores of the Semmerlak and Skarsind mithril heading east to Delev and the Iron Roundtower.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: a new weirwood grove has been discovered in Liathaven.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a Summer proposal would move the Broken Shore Bounty's offices to Siroc, where the Salt Guard could protect them.
t.Mitwold: The Blackfield Market could be built at Blackfield on the road between Meade and Wayford, buying white granite. It would need a Senate motion or wayleave, 12 wains of weirwood, 24 crowns in labour and three months' work.
t.Morrow: Morrow's peaks are a noted source of fallen ilium, though invasion has hurt its prosperity. Its miners could sell mithril and ilium at the proposed Siluri market.
t.Redoubt: Stable Redoubt was chosen by Urizeni architects as the site of a possible national Bourse market for mithril and/or ilium.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was one of four League cities that could host the proposed all-resource market.
t.Semmerholm: Yeofolk of Lacre proposed a quarterly Star Metal Market buying ilium netted from the Semmerlak, overseen by a Starmetal Seneschal.
t.Skarsind: Gulhule is booming again, while struggling Krysse proposed a Miner's Market where an orc bonesetter could buy mithril, rather than see Skarsind's mithril drift east to Varushka.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the constant back-and-forth over Spiral is cited as damaging Urizen's prosperity.
t.Tassato: Tassato was one of four League cities that could host the proposed all-resource market. It is also home to Bishop Imago Monta di Tassato Regario, who suggested an Ombudsman of the Bourse.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was a candidate host for the League market, and its merchants might also trade at the proposed Krysse and Valashal halls.
t.The Semmerlak: Small amounts of ilium drawn from the lake in fishing nets would supply the proposed Star Metal Market at Lacre.
t.Weirwater: A weirwood market-faire was proposed at Applefell, with support pledged by a Seneschal of Spiral Castle, but the Dawnish assembly could not secure a greater majority for it.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Zenith is cited as a blow to Urizen's prosperity.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: A white granite trading hall was proposed at Valashal in south-east Hahnmark, and the Wintermark assembly indicated it would benefit the nation.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: A mithril and/or ilium market was proposed in the foothills of northern Siluri, needing new roads and a bridge.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: Estermark's Gulhule is booming once more, while Krysse proposed a Miner's Market buying mithril, which would need road works.

Improve Reumah's Rest.d: In Autumn 383YE the Senate considered a motion to improve the fortification Reumah's Rest, which stands in the Coursmouth region of Necropolis, a Highguard territory. The motion noted that funds would be required for the work. It was proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Kahraman, but it did not pass, so no upgrade to the fort was commissioned that season.

n.Highguard: The failed motion left Highguard's fortification at Reumah's Rest in its Necropolis territory un-upgraded, although outside senators had pushed for the improvement.

t.Necropolis: The defences of Necropolis did not change, because the proposed upgrade to Reumah's Rest was not approved.

r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Reumah's Rest in Coursmouth was the fort the motion sought to upgrade, but the motion failed and the fortification stayed as it was.

Improve Reumah's Rest II.d: The commission used standard costs: 100 wains of white granite and 200 crowns of labour, taking one year to complete. Marley of Treen made the first contribution after the Autumn Equinox 383YE, giving 6 thrones 2 crowns and 25 wains of white granite. Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Lieselotte van Holberg and small donors added money. Further contributions came after the Winter Solstice 383YE from Ehud and Richardo, after the Winter Solstice 384YE from Nemuel and Asael, and after the Spring Equinox 385YE from Arlais, Daughter of Mari, who gave 24 wains of white granite.

n.Highguard: Highguard stands to gain a stronger defence in Necropolis, with the fortification of Reumah's Rest due to rise to a strength of 6,000 once the upgrade is finished.

t.Necropolis: Reumah's Rest, the fortification in Necropolis, is the subject of the upgrade, funded by donations of white granite and money from Autumn 383YE through Spring 385YE.

In the flat field.d: Lily Guildenstern made the breadbasket available for Marcher festivals. A Marcher Assembly mandate with 25 liao would see households share it with the thralls and invite them to Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland for the harvest, reducing the liao needed for the egregore to bond them. Whittle, which resisted the Jotun for thirty years through Hatred, answered the Assembly's offer through Sally Thatcher with defiance. Priests think about a score of ringleaders hold Whittle together. Options presented: a Senate-ordered magistrates' investigation, a Silent Bell inquiry with grey pilgrims backed by an Assembly of Nine mandate, provoking an uprising for armies to crush, or sanctuary in Tassato. Separately, young thralls who wish to fight may join the Imperial Orcs.

n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Udoo's mandate made clear that any young former thrall who wishes to fight may join the Imperial Orcs, though few are expected to do so; their descendants would come to hear both Imperial Orc and Jotun ancestors.
n.Jotun: The Jotun former thralls of the Mournwold, who honour their ancestors with household harvest shrines, may be invited to feast with Marchers, while the Jotun conquest of Bregasland continues to loom over the Marches.
n.The League: The League's bishops are considering Merchant-Prince Mariana's proposal to offer the Whittle folk sanctuary in Tassato, where some of their kin already live.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly could pass a mandate urging households to share the breadbasket with the thralls, while its offer to let Whittle recant Hatred was flatly refused, forcing a choice over how to deal with the village.

t.Bregasland: Despite the Jotun conquest, Marchers in beleaguered Bregasland celebrate the Wassail in defiance, and the thralls may be invited there as harvest guests; the spirit of wassail could help bring orc and human together if the Military Council chooses to fight at Bill Sabbey.
t.Mitwold: If the breadbasket mandate is passed, Mournwold thralls would be invited to Mitwold as guests for the harvest festival.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold is where the thralls may be welcomed to Wassail feasts, and where the Hate-following village of Whittle stands defiant, facing possible investigation, a Silent Bell hunt, armed suppression or relocation.
t.Tassato: Tassato has been proposed as a sanctuary for the Whittle folk, an option now being discussed by the League's bishops.
t.Upwold: If the breadbasket mandate is passed, Mournwold thralls would be invited to Upwold as guests for the harvest festival.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mestra is home to Little Mournwold, a Marcher enclave of Whittle folk who never returned home, and the proposed destination for those offered sanctuary in Tassato.

In the garden of defiance.d: Most of Holmauer Park withered, though the Imperial Menagerie, the Marcher apple grove and General Flowers' Memorial Garden were spared. Rotting vegetation fouled the waters, and League or Highborn Synod mandates were proposed to fund a clean-up. Rats driven into Holfried raised the Custodian of the Kennels' income by 72 rings a season. The Wunderkind Woods now ooze a sap usable as Winter vis, and the Senate could create titles for this orchard, a souvenir stall at the twisted Sculpture Garden, and an inspiring pavilion on the Looking Glass Lake. A menhir-ringed herb garden was proposed for the Duelling Fields. Rival mandates were also proposed to honour General Flowers or remake her garden for Empress Lisabetta.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as the enemy Holberg held off for thirty years, and their reputation for disease makes the fouled waters more dangerous.
n.Highguard: Ethan of the Gilded Sceptre urged the Highborn Assembly to make amends for the mess their people helped create by funding the clean-up of Holmauer's waters, at the cost of a one-rank production penalty to every Highborn business if enacted.
n.The League: Holberg's foremost park lay blighted, and League merchant-princes, assemblies and senators were offered a mandate to clean its waters, several possible new titles and sinecures, and a mandate to remake the Memorial Garden as a flower garden for Empress Lisabetta.
n.The Marches: The Marcher apple grove and General Flowers' Memorial Garden escaped the curse, and the Marcher Assembly could send pilgrims to honour her there, while a Marcher landskeeper proposed protective menhirs and a herb garden on the Duelling Fields.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as a Highborn territory its businesses would share the one-rank production penalty if the Highborn clean-up mandate were enacted.
t.Holberg: The city suffered the blighting of Holmauer Park and faced fouled waters and a plague of rats, but was offered mandates and Senate titles to clean up and profit from the ruin before the end of the Winter Solstice.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the proposed menhirs drew on plans the late Richard of Holberg drew up to protect the Mourn.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the landskeeper Abigail Ashill, who proposed the menhirs on the Duelling Fields, hails from Ashill in Upwold.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Rats driven out of the cursed park flooded Holfried in numbers unseen since 379YE, boosting demand for Georgie's House ratting dogs, while the Marcher graveyard by its southern wall was untouched.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The park at the heart of Holmauer was cursed, its rivers fouled and the Wunderkind Woods turned into a Winter regio, leaving the sites at the centre of every proposed mandate and title.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Mentioned in passing: Abigail Ashill, the landskeeper who proposed the menhir ring, is described as being of Ashill, Ashbrook.

Large but far away.d: Asavea's Plenum began moving towards an accord with Jarm, and trade with Nemoria suffered a penalty while its temple stood damaged. Imperial captains evacuated defeated rebels, and Marracossans settled in Trajadoz, Torres, where they sought Senate permission for a temple. Commonwealth magicians crowded the Siroc embassy, raising Madruga's taxes. The Commonwealth proposed a schloss by the Lyceum, while Frederick di Sarvos offered his Diora University as an alternative. Jarm cut mana crystal exports, and war with the Commonwealth began after a failed coup in Lantir. Sumaah planned a Synod summit. Sarcophan enclave and Kruidenkenner opportunities would expire at the season's end, and the Gjullit docks offer had already lapsed.

n.Grendel: Under the orders of the Salt Lords, the Grendel still let Asavean merchants dock at the Feroz temple, so the goodwill it once gave Imperial fleet owners now flows to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Felix's Watch of Highguard is named as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Chainbreaker Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea.
n.Navarr: The Sumaah präst Nikolaj Rondtyig has walked the trods with several stridings. He planned to go straight to the Navarr camp at Anvil to consult the Advisor on the Vallorn and hoped to join a foray through the Sentinel Gate.
n.The Brass Coast: Marracossan refugees have settled in Trajadoz in Madruga, and Commonwealth trade through Siroc has raised the territory's prosperity. The Brass Coast also faces a choice over a Commonwealth schloss near the Lyceum.
n.The League: Frederick di Sarvos offered to build his Diora University, which would draw Commonwealth trade to Sarvos. The Tassato Mana Exchange faces reduced Jarmish crystal supplies, and Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato serves as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
n.Varushka: The chance to authorise a Sarcophan enclave at Isember in Karsk, with reciprocal Imperial enclaves in the Delves, would expire at the end of the Autumn Equinox.

t.Feroz: The Asavean temple in Feroz still stands and Asavean merchants still dock there, though its goodwill now benefits the Grendel. The Marracossans cited it when hoping for a temple of their own.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Trajadoz was founded to foster trade between the mines of newly conquered Kahraman and Sarvos.
t.Karsk: A Sarcophan proposal for an enclave at Isember awaited a Senate decision, with a deadline at the end of the Autumn Equinox.
t.Madruga: Marracossan refugees have settled in Trajadoz, and Commonwealth trade through Siroc raised Madruga's taxation by ten Thrones, rising to fifteen if the proposed Lyceum schloss were built. The Gjullit offer to build docks in Siroc has expired.
t.Sarvos: The Sarcophan enclave proposal at the Alivetti estates was extended to the end of the Autumn Equinox. If Frederick di Sarvos's Diora University were built first, Commonwealth trade benefits would flow to Sarvos instead of Madruga.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Trajadoz last swelled with people during the invasion of Segura in 363YE and emptied after its reclamation in 378YE.
t.Tassato: As Jarm stockpiles for war, the Tassato Mana Exchange will see a slight reduction in the mana crystals available from its highest tier.

r.Madruga/Torres: Around a thousand Marracossan refugees have made camp in the largely abandoned town of Trajadoz and wish to stay. They asked for a Senate motion permitting a temple to their three gods, and a separate group set out on pilgrimage to Anvil.

Love and rockets.d: Mael Donjeon of House Remys urged Dawn's troubadours to teach the Highborn about glory and love. Both assemblies ignored the civil service's warning that this could worsen conflicts of faith, and Kerem of the Chantry's welcome passed 269-0. Most troubadours moved their hosts and linked love and glory to the virtues, though some dismissed the virtues entirely. Claims that love and glory should be pre-eminent among the virtues still troubled many Highborn. The Highborn Assembly may pass one of three competing mandates, each needing a Greater majority. Calling love and glory virtuous would bind the nations closer. Calling them a harmless distraction would simply lift the Dawnish congregations' penalty. Calling them a vice would expel the Grey Pilgrims from Dawn and hamper joint military campaigns.

n.Dawn: Dawn's troubadours carried the nation's ideals of love and glory into Highguard and were mostly well received. If the Highborn endorse those ideals as virtuous, Dawnish congregations would gain liao and votes, but if they condemn them, Grey Pilgrims would be barred from Dawn and its armies would struggle to fight alongside Highborn ones.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a Dawnish yeofolk's husband and family were killed by the Druj after the Barrens fell.
n.Highguard: Highborn chapters opened their doors to the Dawnish troubadours, and many were moved by their songs. The Highborn Assembly must now decide whether love and glory are virtuous, merely other qualities, or a vice, with consequences for its kinship with Dawn and for joint military campaigns.

t.Astolat: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Astolat.
t.Bastion: Troubadours sang across Bastion's chapter halls, and many visited Elayne Silverlark's basilica there; a few were allowed to play her mandolin, reviving interest in the proposed Arbour of the Twin Roses.
t.Casinea: Dawnish troubadours spread through Casinea's chapter halls, singing of love and glory and debating the virtues with their Highborn hosts.
t.Necropolis: Dawnish troubadours performed in Necropolis's chapter halls as part of their mission to bring Dawn's understanding of the Way to Highguard.
t.Reikos: Reikos was among the four Highborn territories where Dawnish troubadours sang their songs of love and glory to welcoming chapters.
t.Semmerholm: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Semmerholm.
t.Weirwater: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Weirwater.

Mercy is weakness.d: The Tempest Jade Maiden sect, reconciled with Urizen in 382YE, lost two thirds of its scholars when the Druj attacked the construction site in Morrow. With the temple now complete and backed by the Wisdom Assembly, the scholars challenge Synod priests across the Empire. Any mandate without a greater majority is now ineffective. Recognising Sulemaine as a paragon or exemplar would double the liao a mandate needs. A Urizen Assembly mandate passed with a greater majority could allow new sword scholar temples across Morrow. Opponents led by the sentinel Leoditus urge condemnation, which could open mandates to cast the scholars out.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the nation plays no part, and its only apparent link is the name of the Citadel of the Silver Dawn, where Leoditus teaches.
n.Druj: The Druj had slaughtered two thirds of the sword scholars when they attacked the temple site. Any new sword scholar temples in Morrow would turn their pitiless warriors against them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate encouraging corsairs to raid the Grendel is cited as one that would have failed. The Grendel are also named as a foe any new temples would fight.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate supporting the Great Dance of the Navarr is cited as one that would have failed under the scholars' opposition.
n.Urizen: Urizen's sword scholars, backed by the Wisdom Assembly, now check the whole Synod. The Urizen National Assembly could urge the nation to embrace the Paragon of Blades, though sentinels such as Leoditus argue against them.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the mandate upholding the Wintermark tradition of interring the dead in the Kallavesa marshes is cited as one that would have failed.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate upholding the interment of the dead in the Kallavesa marshes is given as an example of one that would have failed.
t.Morrow: The Temple of the Winds in Morrow is complete and is the scholars' base. A Urizen Assembly mandate with a greater majority could allow more sword scholar temples across Morrow, each defending the territory like a fortification.
t.Redoubt: Sword scholar temples could not be effectively built in Redoubt, where the rival sentinels hold stronger influence and would resist any such effort.

Power, corruption, and lies.d: Urizen astronomancers spotted a conjunction that empowered destructive enchantments and kept part of the Icy Maw curse on Bastion and Casinea alive, disrupting chamber rituals at Anvil. The Conclave's new running order was adopted for the Equinox. Seven magical castles were raised in Hahnmark, Kahraman, Bregasland and Kallavesa, and Cathan Canae sent two bands of frost giants to guard Wintermark's Beacons. Nightly lights over Reikos celebrated the liberation of Tamarbode, Imperial Orcs shared ancestral dreams, and the curse on Zephaniah's Lament lifted. Several territories stayed starless or veiled. Summer eternals, including Sadogua, prepared champions for a new tourney for the Icy Crag. Prospero, Callidus, Sorin, Lashonar and Sung offered various opportunities.

n.Dawn: Dawnish troubadours sought out the story of Zephaniah's Lament and wrote songs about the League heroes of Tamarbode, while Adamant was expected to look for tourney champions among the Dawnish and Semmerholm's skies stayed starless.
n.Druj: The Druj-held Zenith and the Barrens remained under inky starless skies, which impeded divination on them and strengthened the secretiveness of any naga who had spent time there.
n.Grendel: Grendel-held Spiral stayed starless and shrouded against divination, and former gladiators of Mareave were helped by the orc dreams to settle into Imperial Orc society.
n.Highguard: The Highborn suffered the after-effects of the Icy Maw curse on Bastion and Casinea and watched three months of celebratory lights over Reikos, while the curse and long malaise over the chapter of Zephaniah's Lament finally lifted.
n.Imperial Orcs: For three months every Imperial Orc dreamed of their nation's history and achievements and woke refreshed and proud, which especially helped the newly joined gladiators of Mareave and slaves of Dubhtraig to integrate.
n.Jotun: Magical castles in Hahnmark, Kahraman and Bregasland stood against Jotun advances, notably impeding them in the Marches, and Cathan Canae's frost giants now guard Wintermark's Beacons against them.
n.The Brass Coast: A castle of white stone and black ice was raised over Serra Briante, certain Freeborn were summoned to honour an old bargain with Callidus, and Sung set Maya of the Brass Coast a riddle challenge.
n.The League: League armies and independent captains were celebrated nightly over Reikos for liberating Tamarbode, the stars returned over Holberg, and the Highborn chapter that cursed Sarvos and Holberg saw two members declared sorcerers.
n.The Marches: The Sussivari Frost Coven's castle of fog and water over North Fens significantly slowed the Jotun advance into Bregasland.
n.Thule: Penumbral Veils were reported over Thule-held Otkodov's regions of Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld, and over Verthandi, impeding divination there.
n.Urizen: Urizen astronomancers were first to notice the conjunction, which held particular meaning for them, Adamant was expected to seek tourney champions from Urizen, and the Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch received an invitation to Prospero's game.
n.Varushka: Ossium's skies stayed starless and some Varushkans, citing the recent Synod mandate, wondered aloud about the nature of Zephaniah's Lament's deal with Skathe.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained castles in Hahnmark and Kallavesa and two bands of Summer frost giants to guard its Beacons in honour of three of its heroes, the Kallavesi were invited to share the Raven's Dream at Ishal, and Shaman's curse coins passed to his supporters.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named on the page; the only Dawnish connections are travelling troubadours and Adamant's interest in Dawnish champions.
t.Bastion: Bastion endured a season of the Icy Maw curse, with halved mana yields, foul weather and uneasy magicians, and its lingering power reached Anvil thanks to the conjunction.
t.Bregasland: A castle of fog and water raised over North Fens by the Sussivari Frost Coven significantly impeded the Jotun advance into the territory.
t.Casinea: Casinea suffered the Icy Maw curse alongside Bastion, with weakened magic, halved mana sites, harsh weather and troubled magicians.
t.Hahnmark: Three castles of ice and granite were raised in Hahnmark's hills, and five score frost giants arrived to defend its Beacons until Summer 384YE.
t.Holberg: The darkness that hid Holberg's stars faded, which some credited to Juha the Cave Spider, after last season's curse by Zephaniah's Lament had withered Holmauer Park.
t.Kahraman: A castle of white stone and black ice was raised over Serra Briante, and it would have troubled the Jotun had they not retreated from the hills above Damata.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa received five score frost giants to guard its Beacons and a castle of fog and water over West Marsh, and Ishal's mystics invited the Kallavesi to share the Raven's Dream there.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the gladiators of Mareave are noted as among the newest Imperial Orcs whom the ancestral dreams helped to integrate.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's agent who delivered the notice of the new trials is known as Ania of Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Ossium's night skies stayed starless, which impeded divination and gave naga who had spent time there a strong urge towards secrecy.
t.Otkodov: Penumbral Veils hung over Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld in Otkodov, impeding divination on the territory.
t.Reikos: Glowing lights celebrating the League's liberation of Tamarbode filled Reikos's skies every night for three months, delighting children and visiting troubadours but wearying many Highborn.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the transformation of Sarvos after its destruction is cited as a possible reflection of the conjunction, and the city is named as a target of the Zephaniah's Lament curse.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's skies remained starless, impeding divination and intensifying the secretiveness of naga who had spent time there.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Hahnmark castles were meant to make that territory harder for the Jotun to conquer than Sermersuaq had been.
t.Spiral: Spiral stayed under inky starless skies, impeding divination there and strengthening naga secretiveness.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens remained starless, with divination impeded and naga who had stayed there gripped by an urge for secrecy.
t.Verthandi: Verthandi was reported to lie under a Penumbral Veil that impeded divination.
t.Zenith: Zenith's skies remained inky black, impeding divination and affecting naga who had spent time there.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and water over North Fens, which significantly slowed the Jotun advance.
r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: The Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a castle of ice and granite in Kalpamark against any Jotun push south.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: A castle of ice and granite was raised in Northspires by the Voices of the Unbound Storm.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: Valasmark gained a castle of ice and granite called from the Breath of Winter by the Voices of the Unbound Storm.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Mentioned in passing: the withering of Holmauer Park is recalled as part of the earlier curse by Zephaniah's Lament.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Summer Dawning Relentless raised a castle of white stone and black ice over Serra Briante, which would have hampered the Jotun had they not withdrawn.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: A Sentinel Gate conjunction was to open in the marshes near Ishal in Skymark on Friday night, so the Kallavesi mystics could share the Raven's Dream and meet the mystics of Ishal.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and water over West Marsh.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Nithoggir was reported to lie under a Penumbral Veil that impeded divination.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Sküld was reported to be shrouded by a Penumbral Veil that blocked divination.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Imperial merchants reported that the Penumbral Veil still hung over Urdur.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: The League's destruction of the Garden of Llofir and liberation of Tamarbode was celebrated by three months of nightly lights over Reikos.

Ratify treaty with the Axos Autumn 383YE.d: The treaty, presented as such after discussion with the Constitutional Court, contained five points. The Empire would provide maps of the Mountains of the Moon and let Axos use the Sarangrave spy network. Axou military captains would be invited to defend the Eastern Brokerage in Therunin. Students from the College in Maykop could apply to Imperial centres of learning, and the Axou ambassador could buy land at the Quayside in Issyk. The Military Council approved the military aspects. The treaty could not extend Therunin's offer of payment to the Axou, because those rewards come from private citizens and the Senate cannot direct how citizens spend their wealth. The claim that points could be combined to save Senate time was also ruled invalid.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the treaty grants Axos use of the Sarangrave spy network, which operates in Druj-held land.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Therunin proposed the treaty, which invited Axou captains to help defend the Eastern Brokerage. Whether to pay those Axou soldiers is left to the Navarr citizens of Therunin.

t.Mountains of the Moon: The Empire agreed to give Axos maps of the Mountains of the Moon, which were held by the Tsark at the time.
t.Sarangrave: Axos was permitted to use the Imperial spy network in the Sarangrave, which was held by the Druj that season.
t.Therunin: Axou military captains were invited to defend the Eastern Brokerage in Therunin. The treaty could not extend the territory's privately funded rewards to them, so that choice rests with its Navarr citizens.

Ratify treaty with the Grendel Autumn 38.d: Proposed by Madruga and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the treaty passed. It established peace for two years, to be renegotiated at the Spring Equinox 385YE. The Grendel agreed not to trade with or materially assist the Druj, and to release one Imperial slave for each day the treaty holds. The Empire ceded Afarjasse and Morajasse in Feroz and Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral, and agreed to build no shipyards or navies in the Bay of Catazar. Citizens in the ceded regions had two seasons to relocate with their possessions. Both sides renounced raiding, and disputes go first to ambassadors. The Grendel became foreigners, and raiding Grendel vessels or attacking the Broken Shore became illegal.

n.Druj: The Grendel agreed not to trade with the Druj or give them any material assistance in their war against the Empire, cutting off a potential source of support.
n.Grendel: The Grendel gained five Imperial regions and two years of peace, in return for releasing Imperial slaves, refusing aid to the Druj and giving up raids. Under Imperial law they are now foreigners rather than enemies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast lost Afarjasse and Morajasse in Feroz to the Grendel, and its citizens there had two seasons to relocate. Its captains may no longer raid Grendel ships or attack the Broken Shore.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral to the Grendel, and its citizens there were given two seasons' grace to move into Imperial territory with their possessions.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Empire agreed to build no shipyards or navies in the Bay of Catazar while the treaty lasts, and raiding between the Empire and the Grendel is forbidden.
t.Feroz: Two of Feroz's regions, Afarjasse and Morajasse, were ceded to the Grendel, leaving the territory partly in orc hands.
t.Spiral: Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral were ceded to the Grendel, formalising their control of much of the territory.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse was ceded to the Grendel. Imperial citizens living there had two seasons to leave with their possessions.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Morajasse was ceded to the Grendel, and its Imperial residents were given two seasons to relocate to Imperial territory.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra was handed to the Grendel under the treaty, with two seasons' grace for Imperial citizens to depart.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ateri was ceded to the Grendel. Its Imperial citizens were allowed two seasons to relocate with their belongings.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion was ceded to the Grendel, and Imperial citizens there had two seasons to move into Imperial lands.

Ratify treaty with the Sarcophan Delves.d: The treaty, proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Segura, ceded the Alivetti estate in Sarvos to the Sarcophan Delves, to be granted to the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vandersaar for their use. In return, the Huisbaas agreed to preserve the tomb ruins of Empress Giselle as a historic landmark and to pay 4 rings of ilium each season to the Imperial holder of the Steel Fist bourse seat for as long as the land remained conceded. The Huisbaas also undertook to provide land within the Buitenlandsewijk, in keeping with the Constitution, for Imperial construction. The Empire agreed to build a Temple of the Way there at a time of its choosing.

n.The League: A League territory lost the Alivetti estate to a foreign enclave. The tomb of Empress Giselle there was protected as a historic landmark, and the Empire gained land within the Buitenlandsewijk for a Temple of the Way.

t.Sarvos: The Alivetti estate in Sarvos was conceded to the Sarcophan Delves for the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vandersaar, who undertook to preserve Empress Giselle's tomb ruins as a historic landmark and to pay the Empire 4 rings of ilium each season.

Rise of Terunael.d: The Heirs have largely abandoned Brocéliande and now aim to stir the vallornspawn rather than spread the vallorn. About sixty gathered around Deer's Folly in Hercynia, aided by the Varushkan Cabal of the Green Mother. About fifty were in Therunin, backed by Urizeni idolaters from Greenfountain Spire who attacked Peakedge Stead and were repulsed. Rivers Run Red was cast on Hercynia, Therunin and Liathaven, but the Great Forest Orcs broke it in Therunin. Captains and armies could defend each territory, and the outcome depended on the strength committed. Further Synod action against Yaw'nagrah idolaters was also proposed.

n.Highguard: A Highborn investigator of the Silent Bell helped uncover the plot, and Chalcis Mount in Reikos could be threatened if the vallornspawn ravage Therunin unchecked.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind could see vallornspawn spill over from Hercynia if the defence there fails badly.
n.Jotun: The Jotun holding Liathaven seem unaware of the threat and would bear most casualties if it goes undefended. Warning them might prompt a defence, while a massacre might make them abandon the territory.
n.Navarr: Navarr steadings in Hercynia, Therunin and Liathaven face imminent vallornspawn attacks stirred by briar traitors. Treji, Peakedge Stead and the Thimble are at risk, as are the treasury contributions of the threatened territories.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named as probably safe because Wither the Seed keeps Liathaven's vallornspawn sluggish.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold and Bregasland are judged probably safe, and recent events in Bregasland make it hard for armies to enter Liathaven defensively.
n.Thule: Around a score of Heirs reportedly headed into southern Sküld in Otkodov, where a vallorn slumbers, and it is unknown whether the Thule know of it or how they would respond.
n.Urizen: A Urizeni coven from Greenfountain Spire in Peregro was exposed as long-standing idolaters of Yaw'nagrah after attacking Peakedge Stead alongside the Heirs.
n.Varushka: The Cabal of the Green Mother from northern Volodmartz was traced into Hercynia, and vallornspawn raised in Sküld could in theory come west into Volodmartz.
n.Wintermark: The mountains shield Hahnmark from direct threat for now, though unchecked chaos in Hercynia could send vallornspawn as far as Kalpamark.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: listed as probably safe from Liathaven's vallornspawn, and recent developments there hinder armies entering Liathaven defensively.
t.Brocéliande: After their defeat here the Heirs have largely abandoned Brocéliande, which remains under Wither the Seed and is covered by separate Winds of Fortune.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is not thought to be directly threatened yet, but vallornspawn could spill in if Hercynia's defence fails badly.
t.Hercynia: The main gathering of Heirs is rousing ettercaps and vallornspawn under Rivers Run Red. Treji, the Heartwood of the Great Vale and the territory's resources face heavy damage unless over 20,000 strength defends it.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: named as probably safe because Liathaven's vallornspawn are too sluggish to spread.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: named as probably safe from Liathaven's sluggish vallornspawn for the moment.
t.Liathaven: Heirs and Children of Yaw'nagrah operate openly here under Rivers Run Red, which no one is there to remove. The few remaining Navarr and the unaware Jotun face vallornspawn attacks, and the Empire must rely on military units rather than armies to help.
t.Morrow: Sentinels and briar magicians from Morrow's Greenfountain Spire were revealed as Yaw'nagrah idolaters who joined the Heirs' assault in Therunin.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: listed among territories probably safe from Liathaven's vallornspawn.
t.Otkodov: Unverified reports say Heirs of Terunael entered southern Sküld, so the threat they pose for now seems confined to Thule lands.
t.Reikos: Reikos could be threatened at Chalcis Mount if Therunin's vallornspawn are left rampant.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind could suffer vallornspawn incursions if the defence of Hercynia falls short.
t.Therunin: Heirs backed by Yaw'nagrah's idolaters are rousing vallornspawn, giant insects and a marshwalker. Rivers Run Red was broken by the Great Forest Orcs, but the Docks at Feverwater, Peakedge Stead, the Thimble and the Holt of the Oak hang on the strength of the defence.
t.Volodmartz: The Cabal of the Green Mother hails from northern Volodmartz, Heirs passed through Suvretz, and vallornspawn from Sküld could conceivably come west.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the opportunity to clear the vallorn from Dark Ranging is referred to another Wind of Fortune.
r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Vallornspawn could venture as far as Kalpamark if the chaos in Hercynia is allowed to spread.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: Up to sixty Heirs were confirmed around the borders of this vallorn region, with expeditions deep inside rousing its ettercaps and vallornspawn.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: Northpines is relatively secure in its mountains and is offering ingots to captains who help defend Hercynia.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: Old Ranging is seriously threatened by the vallornspawn because Deer's Folly lies at the centre of the territory.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: A steading in Summersend has already been assaulted, and the region remains seriously threatened.
r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: A striding was decimated here while pausing on the vallorn's borders, and the region faces further danger.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: The threat is gathering under the eaves of Liath's Heart, unnoticed by the Jotun.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Idolatrous mages and sentinels came down from Peregro to attack Therunin, and Peregro could itself be threatened if Therunin's vallornspawn run unchecked.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: A score or so Heirs reportedly entered southern Sküld, where a vallorn slumbers, possibly with Yaw'nagrah's help.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Chalcis Mount may be threatened by vallornspawn if the defence of Therunin fails.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Great Forest Orcs here were warned of the danger, broke the Rivers Run Red curse with Rivers of Life and are readying the Spears of the Pine to guard their settlements and the Holt of the Oak.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Stead repulsed an attack by Urizeni idolaters and heralds of Yaw'nagrah, but it and the Eastern Broker's offices remain at risk.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Most of the attackers on Peakedge Stead escaped back into Sweetglades.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: Heirs of Terunael were reportedly seen heading north-east out of Suvretz towards Sküld.

Small but nearby.d: Axos remains the only Liberty Pact signatory. An Ilarch, Penthesil Lerophon, claimed descent from Kaban and sought Imperial aid, chiefly white granite, money and recognition, to rebuild the Tunnels of Kaban. Trade at Kantor stayed disrupted after the end of slavery. Freed orcs in Axos remain heavily restricted, and Snowbound Dukka urged a Synod statement calling on Imperial Orc captains to help them flee. The Modnos family reportedly offered 10 thrones for each heart of Livia, Astrid and Lord Colwynn. Smuggling rumours persisted, and survivors of an attacked Faraden caravan were escorted to Damata. The Iron Confederacy kept its embargo, but Ser Pippin Lavasse planned a Winter visit and two Hand of Dumon priests were travelling to Anvil.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were driven from the Tunnels of Kaban in 380YE, and Axos fears that freed orcs might join them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Axos fears that freed orcs might join the Grendel, and poor maps of the Grendel territory of Mareave block any overland escape route.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Hand of Dumon delegation joined a merchant caravan bound for Casinea on its way to Anvil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Snowbound Dukka, a preacher from the Legion's Rookery, called on Imperial Orc priests to raise a Statement of Principle. It would urge Imperial Orc ship captains to help any orc who wishes to escape Axos.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn lands bore the brunt of events: rumoured Faraden smuggling through Segura and Kahraman, invasions in Feroz and Segura, and a land border to the Confederacy that stays closed. It was also suggested that the Freeborn National Assembly raise a statement about the smuggling.
n.The League: Erasmo di Tassato of the League is Ambassador to Faraden, and the Sarvos embassy serves as the landing point for Iron Confederacy visitors. The Sarvos thief-taker Maria Giacora also weighed in on the smuggling.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as one of the smaller nations near the Empire, but no developments there are described.
n.Urizen: Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen is Ambassador to Axos. The Hand of Dumon delegation, invited by Pallidius of Highwatch's statement, will go first to the Highwatch camp in Urizen to discuss the Way.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Vladimir Sasha Volkov of Varushka is the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy whom Ser Pippin Lavasse intends to meet.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: it is not named, though the page refers to Imperial ships trading at Kantor and the closure of Robec to Imperial vessels.
t.Casinea: The Hand of Dumon delegates were travelling with a merchant caravan into Casinea, bound for Anvil.
t.Feroz: Feroz is under invasion, which forced Ser Pippin Lavasse to travel by sea. The Suranni priests Florent Chappuis and Abélia Gaubert crossed the border here.
t.Kahraman: Southern Kahraman is rumoured to be a Faraden smuggling route. A Green Shield patrol found a battered Faraden caravan in a disused mine in the south west and escorted the survivors to Damata.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Hand of Dumon delegates travelled through Madruga before taking ship to Sarvos.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller nearby nations under Imperial trade sanctions, but no specific developments are described.
t.Sarvos: The Iron Confederacy embassy in Sarvos is the arrival point for Ser Pippin Lavasse and was a stop for the Hand of Dumon delegates. Rumours there suggest Ser Pippin's early notice is meant to ensure his meeting goes ahead.
t.Segura: Segura is under invasion. Northern Segura is also rumoured to be a route for Faraden smugglers, though this remains unconfirmed.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Snowbound Dukka, who is calling for help for Axou orcs, teaches at the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind.

r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Survivors of a Faraden caravan attacked in a disused mine said they were bound for the town of Damata. A Green Shield patrol escorted them there with their dead and a strange symbol daubed on their wagons.

Something must break.d: Sadogua's consumption of the Night technique left a crack in the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic. If Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo is performed on Saturday night of the coming summit, with 7 rings of ilium and the general's consent, Cyclic Magic would become Highest Discipline: five techniques, one per season, each usable once a year. Canterspire, ceded to Phaleron, became the Grand Library, which underpins Urizen Lore, though it contains no rituals yet. The Doyen of the Spires' codification of Regrow the Land's Heart has slowed to 15 a season since Spiral was lost, and alternative versions are suggested. Adamant sends Galene Netherwatch a gift, and mandates promoting virtuous cooperation with eternals are proposed.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's enchanters are cited as having long and profitable experience of dealing with eternals.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the foe the Highborn armies held back from Morrow after the fall of Zenith.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the page notes Spiral has been lost to Urizen again, slowing the Doyen of the Spires, but does not name Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Three Watchers memorialise three Highborn armies that helped Urizeni flee Zenith, and Highguard is described as cautious about dealing with eternals.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: some astronomancers link the conjunction to events in Sarvos, where destruction is becoming a chance for something new.
n.Urizen: Urizen may transform the Citadel Guard's magic into Highest Discipline, now has its own national lore anchored by the Grand Library of Canterspire, and its assembly could pass a mandate opening Winter opportunities to work with eternals.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan cabalists are cited as having long and profitable experience of treating with creatures of the realms.

t.Morrow: The Three Watchers, giant statues raised by Adamant's koboldi, guard the approach to Morrow from Zenith and honour the Highborn armies who defended it. Adamant has now sent a token of esteem in recognition of that work.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the unmade trove that empowered the Citadel Guard was originally found beneath the Unmade spire in Redoubt.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: astronomancers point to Sarvos as a place where an ending wrought by destruction is being turned into an opportunity for something new.
t.Spiral: The loss of Spiral cut the Doyen's codification rate to 15 a season. Regrow the Land's Heart, a planned year-long Spring enchantment to heal Spiral's war scars, might be reworked to target any territory.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Zenith have swelled Canterspire, and the Three Watchers look out over the approach from Zenith to Morrow.

r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Tomari, and refers to Redoubt only as the place where the unmade trove was found beneath the Unmade spire.

The DOOM that came to Sarvos.d: The curse left no lingering magic, but a deep malaise and fear of doom took hold. Three follies were proposed, each able to underpin a League Assembly mandate giving Sarvos a new epithet: Bethany Gustava von Sarvos's renovation of the Glass Palace (City of Songs), Genia Bourné's Night Masks fashion school (City of Masks), and Martina di Sarvos's Greatest Taste banqueting hall (City of Spices). If none is completed before Autumn 384YE, Sarvos may become the Doomed or Sinking City. Fire-safety commissions were also proposed. Husks from the Iron Helms were going missing and a winter regio appeared in the Caricomare sewers. Eduardo von Tassato sought a meeting of reckoners.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: wild rumours in the League cities speak of curses being levied against Highguard's territories in retaliation, and the city's founding is dated to before the wars between the patricians and the chapters of Highguard.
n.The League: The League faces a choice over Sarvos's identity, with the Senate able to commission one or more follies and the League Assembly then able to mandate a new epithet for the city. Its reckoners are also being summoned by Eduardo von Tassato, likely to discuss a reckoning for the curses on Sarvos and Holberg.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the attack on Holberg is referenced alongside Sarvos as one of the two curses fuelling calls for a reckoning, and architect Bethany Gustava von Sarvos studied there.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos lost every mirror, including its famed rooftop mirrors, and must complete a commission defining its new character before Autumn 384YE or risk lasting doom. Meanwhile corpses and a winter regio haunt the Caricomare sewers, with the Iron Helms and Wolves of War stationed nearby.

The blessing way.d: League and Imperial Orc mandates gave the Sand Fishers shelter, a school and a hospital, and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg found them receptive to the Virtues. The Druj then invaded Holberg and offered to release one Imperial captive for each Sand Fisher handed back. Some Sand Fishers hid at Grafflers Old Camp, now apparently a tulpa's lair. The Jotun accepted weregild but refused passage through Sermersuaq, saying any hall should stand empty in Skarsind. Thule took the Sungold Pass, built forts in Bonewood and Krevsaty, and arranged deliveries of freed slaves and Navarr artisans. Grendel Speaker Morna sailed to Sarvos to meet the Imperial Fleet Master.

n.Druj: The Druj invaded Holberg, apparently to punish the Sand Fishers for fleeing. Through a terrified Utterlund youth they offered to free one tormented Imperial citizen for every Sand Fisher returned to them.
n.Grendel: Speaker Morna and a Stone Born guard arrived at Sarvos under a flag of truce and travelled to Anvil to meet Imperial Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, protected by Imperial law throughout.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel delegation travelled through the Highborn territory of Casinea on its way to Anvil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Rykana carried Imperial Orc support to the Sand Fishers and preached hope beyond the Howling Abyss. Consul Skywise Fal's embassy request was redirected by the Jotun to a hall in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Jotun settled the blood-price for the Meeting Place but refused safe passage or an embassy, saying the war would continue. Meanwhile escaped thralls and unknown hunters were striking at their holdings in Sermersuaq, and their mana-gathering drew Imperial attention.
n.Navarr: Under the Thule treaty, the Navarr artisans taken at the fall of Treji were to be delivered to Skogei before winter. Winterfolk ex-thralls also intended to trade their looted goods with the Navarr.
n.The League: Leonora van Holberg rallied Holberg's citizens to support the Sand Fishers, and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg taught them the Virtues. League lands now faced a Druj invasion, while Sarvos received the Grendel envoy.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold orcs are noted as covered elsewhere, and the former thralls there are compared to the Sand Fishers in their belief in reincarnation.
n.Thule: The Thule took the Sungold Pass, set out how slaves would be released for payment, kept their promise to defend Ossium and built new fortresses. They planned to reduce their Ossium presence temporarily to deal with a matter in Sküld.
n.Varushka: Varushkan Yevgeni Katzev served as Ambassador to Otkodov and must sign the payments for freed slaves. Varushkan observers and Karsk wardens reported on Thule activity, and freed slaves could be delivered to Varushkan lands.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark-mediated weregild closed the matter of the Meeting Place. The Jotun delivered their refusal at Atalaq, while thralls sought out Hendel Hearth and the Wintermark egregore found Sentinel Gate conjunctions into Sermersuaq.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Speaker Morna's Grendel delegation travelled through Casinea along the Blood Red Roads.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is not named; its only link is that Navarr artisans taken at Treji are to be returned under the Thule treaty.
t.Holberg: Holberg's citizens poured support into the newly settled Sand Fishers, but a major Druj force invaded the territory to punish them, and the Druj demanded the orcs' return.
t.Karsk: Karsk wardens reported a completed Thule fortification in the hills of Krevsaty, and Ivarsgard was named as a delivery point for freed Imperial slaves.
t.Miekarova: Wendell's Hope in Miekarova was named as one of the places where the Thule would deliver freed Imperial slaves as payments arrived.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold orcs are covered elsewhere, and their former Jotun thralls are compared to the Sand Fishers.
t.Ossium: The Thule kept their bargain to defend Ossium, patrolling its eastern borders alongside three Imperial armies and completing a fortress in the Bonewood. They planned a temporary reduction of their forces after the Equinox.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov ratified a treaty trading Imperial land slaves and Navarr artisans for the Sungold Pass, though it raised questions over one section. It agreed staged payments through the City of Gold and Lead.
t.Sarvos: A Grendel ship in Asavean style docked at Sarvos under a flag of truce, carrying Speaker Morna on his way to Anvil.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun refused Imperial passage through Sermersuaq. Escaped thralls offered Imperial heroes a strike against high-status Jotun, Naeve-marked attacks plagued occupied halls, and thralls were forced to gather mana under guard.
t.Skarsind: The Jotun proposed that any Imperial meeting hall be built in Pakaanan's Pass, and Skogei was chosen to receive the returned Navarr artisans and freed slaves.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted to have invaded Spiral just long enough to do something with the Black Plateau.
t.The Barrens: The Druj had beaten back an invasion of the Barrens, and the civil service advised that handing over the Sand Fishers would mean forcing the tribe into the Barrens.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Some three thousand Sand Fishers settled in Misericorde with shelters, a school and a hospital, but now hid from the Druj. Their missing musicians were heard at Grafflers Old Camp, apparently a tulpa's lair reachable by a Sentinel Gate conjunction.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Druj shadows woke young Micha di Holberg in a forest cabin in Utterlund to carry their offer to the Senate. Micha refused to return home and enlisted with the Holberg garrison.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Warden fellowships reported that the Thule had completed a fortification in the hills of Krevsaty, apparently using the Immaculate Architect.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mentioned in passing: Mieriada is not named, though Wendell's Hope in Miekarova is listed as a delivery point for freed slaves.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: A brand new Thule fortress was completed in the Bonewood in six months, and Grand Warlock Fljajokull came down from there to confer with Imperial captains at Lormaa.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: the Thule said something had come up in Sküld requiring their attention, prompting a temporary drawdown from Ossium.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Mentioned in passing: Sealtoq is not named; the page speaks only of Sermersuaq generally, including a raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears in the north.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at Asiaat's Hollow in Stark offered heroes access near a former Wintermark hall where thralls were gathering mana for the Jotun.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at Stag Fount in Suaq Fount offered heroes a chance to disrupt Jotun mana-gathering near a former Wintermark hall.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Jotun said any Imperial meeting hall should be built in Pakaanan's Pass, but warned it would stand empty until they chose to talk as equals.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Skogei was named as the place where the Thule would deliver the Navarr artisans before winter and where freed Imperial slaves could be handed over.

The lights of Temeschwar.d: Angered by the curses on Sarvos and Holberg, Merchant-Prince Alexi di Temeschwar of the Guild of Lanterneers offered 300 thrones, hoping others would add to it, if the Senate relinquished the Fortress of Salt as a League national seat. The Constitutional Court confirmed it could be appointed by vote or by auction, but relinquishment awaits a new Throne. Bishop Beagan Locular proposed a true-liao memorial to Ratibor in one of three possible sites, while bishops disputed whether his virtue was Ambition or Vigilance. Yermolay Lopakin urged historical research first. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a way into an unexplored cavern beneath Mellfort.

n.Highguard: The Highborn were widely blamed for the curses on Sarvos and Holberg, and the Highborn chapter of the Heirs of Lepidus could be encouraged to complete their study of Ratibor through a statement of principle.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: some scholars believe Mellfort was destroyed in conflict between the Ushka and the ancestors of the Navarr.
n.The League: League citizens could contribute to a purse to buy the Fortress of Salt as a national seat, the National Assembly was asked to state whether Bourse seats should be auctioned or voted on, and League bishops could settle Ratibor's virtue by competing mandates.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's Varushkan roots are recalled, and Alexi's bid drew on a proposal by Oksana Lyava Pinavora and her patriotic boyars and merchants.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the rise of the White City in Bastion is said to have drawn pilgrims away from Mellfort in the past.
t.Holberg: The attacks on Holberg, including the destruction of Holmauer Park, were seen in Temeschwar as an affront to the League, and the Fortress of Salt proposal was discussed in its salons.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: travellers on the road from Temeschwar to Vorota in Karov reported being watched by half-seen figures in the woods of Metri.
t.Sarvos: The curse-driven attacks on Sarvos spurred the Temeschwari to act, and the Fortress of Salt proposal was debated in Sarvos's salons.
t.Temeschwar: Its guilds sought the Fortress of Salt, its bishops weighed building a memorial to Ratibor at Ratibor's Gate, the Red Tower or a city gate, and Mellfort offered a mysterious cavern to explore.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: If auctioning League Bourse seats proved profitable, the method could have implications for how the Great Pits of Ennerlund are appointed.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of Holmauer Park is cited as a sign that League cities cannot afford complacency.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Mentioned in passing: Hanuri is not named directly and is covered only as part of the wider Temeschwar territory.
r.Temeschwar/Locul: A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered ten people a way into an unexplored cavern beneath Mellfort, whose grief-easing aura has drawn pilgrims and would-be exploiters alike.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: Its forests remained haunted by spirits that tore apart bandits but had not harmed honest travellers.
r.Temeschwar/Vargat: Mentioned in passing: the scholar-priest Yermolay Lopakin, who urged research into Ratibor, hails from the village of Tornvale in Vargat.

Three soldiers.d: The Urizen coven Ashen Flame performed The Three Watchers at the Spring Equinox, calling in a boon from Adamant. Aurum of the Nightingale Temple consecrated the shrine with an aura of Loyalty. Highborn or Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow against attack from Zenith, gain 20% and take 10% fewer casualties. Druj patrols flee at the sight of the statues. Until the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Highborn military units cost one less mithril to upgrade and Highborn armies receive extra natural resupply. The Highborn assembly may pass one of two competing mandates, each needing a greater majority, granting either the Crusading Storm or the Put them to the Sword order.

n.Druj: Druj patrols turn and flee at the sight of the Three Watchers, unable to bear the statues and their Loyalty aura. A proposed Highborn mandate would give Highborn armies a merciless Put them to the Sword order aimed specifically at the Druj.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims are flocking to the statues. Until the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Highborn armies recover twice as fast and military units cost one less mithril to upgrade. The assembly has one season to choose between the Crusading Storm and Put them to the Sword orders, and either mandate needs a greater majority.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Feroz hear of the statues and are heartened.
n.Urizen: Urizen commissioned the statues as thanks for Highborn sacrifice. Urizeni armies attacking Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow from Zenith, gain a morale bonus to territory and suffer fewer casualties.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Ossium are cited as an example of how ruling by fear weakens a people's virtue over time.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Brocéliande have their spirits lifted by news of the statues.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Feroz have their spirits lifted by news of the statues.
t.Morrow: The Three Watchers guard the High Pass from Morrow. Highborn and Urizen armies attacking Zenith from here, or defending Morrow against attack from Zenith, gain 20% and take 10% fewer casualties.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Ossium are given as an example of how fear erodes a people's virtue.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is recalled as the first place where Highborn soldiers lost family and friends to the Druj.
t.Zenith: The statues watch over the High Pass into Druj-held Zenith. Highborn and Urizen armies attacking from Morrow gain a bonus, and Druj patrols flee rather than approach the pass.

Woven as a weapon.d: Graciana warned that the trods are a centuries-old, refined solution with no easy gains, and their effect cannot be measured with Day magic. She rejected tearing up the Empire's roads as economically ruinous. She proposed instead a wayhouse programme costing 300 wains of white granite, 100 of weirwood and 100 thrones, taking 18 months and two commissions. It would raise trod traffic by a tenth, enrich Navarr businesses and create five ministry wayhouses. A General Assembly mandate invoking the late Empress's call to pilgrimage could roughly double trod walkers for five years, at a cost in armies and taxes. Her third, riskier idea awaits Aquillian, who is forbidden from ritual magic.

n.Dawn: A proposed wayhouse at Rucastle in Semmerholm, beside Brocéliande, would bring Navarr-run ministry traffic into Dawnish land. If the pilgrimage mandate were endorsed, Dawn would lose a tenth of its taxation for five years, and an army if it can support more than two.
n.Highguard: The Highborn grey pilgrimage has already greatly boosted the trods and was the model for the proposed mandate. Highguard would be spared the mandate's losses of taxation and armies because its people already walk the trods.
n.Imperial Orcs: A wayhouse is proposed at Torfast in Skarsind, at the centre of the northern trade network. The Imperial Orcs would also face reduced taxation, and possibly a lost army, if the pilgrimage mandate passed.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the opening story describes the Jotun as having been driven off the trod, and they hold Liathaven, where the proposals aim to aid Navarr travel and vallorn clearance.
n.Navarr: The appraisal concerns the Navarr's own ancient weapon against the vallorn. The wayhouse programme would enrich Navarr businesses and create five Navarr Imperial positions. A mass pilgrimage could let the Empire clear the vallorn hearts of Hercynia, Liathaven and perhaps Therunin, if enough armies were committed, while sparing Navarr its costs.
n.The League: The League would lose a tenth of its taxation, and an army if it can support more than two, under the proposed pilgrimage mandate. Tassato's La Redotta Rezia is cited as an example of a better-suited appraisal.
n.The Marches: A wayhouse is proposed at Sarcombe in the Mournwold to support trods into Liathaven. The Marches would face reduced taxation, and possibly a lost army, if the pilgrimage mandate were endorsed.
n.Urizen: The Urizen stargazer Aquillian Effugere is the only magician Graciana will trust with her unorthodox plan, but his conviction as a sorcerer may bar him legally. A proposed wayhouse at Peakedge Song could support trods towards Axos, and Urizen would bear the mandate's costs if it passed.

t.Brocéliande: The year-long campaign against the vallorn here inspired Graciana's experimental idea. Navarr businesses connected to Brocéliande would prosper from new wayhouses, with one proposed nearby at Rucastle.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia seconded the motion. The wayhouse programme would bring its businesses an estimated extra 1300 rings each season, and a mass pilgrimage could see its vallorn heart cleared completely.
t.Liathaven: Wayhouses would bring prosperity to Navarr businesses here, and three of the five planned ministry wayhouses would support travel to and from Liathaven. A mass pilgrimage could allow its vallorn heart to be cleared.
t.Miaren: Miaren, the territory already freed by destroying its vallorn heart, would gain less from the wayhouses because the Blood Red Roads already provide some of their benefits.
t.Mournwold: A substantial wayhouse is proposed at Sarcombe to support trods leading into Liathaven.
t.Semmerholm: A substantial wayhouse, operating as a ministry, is proposed at Rucastle, adjacent to Brocéliande.
t.Skarsind: A substantial wayhouse is proposed at Torfast, the centre point of the northern trade network.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: an appraisal on profitably disposing of La Redotta Rezia is given as an example of a more suitable use of appraisal.
t.Therunin: Therunin proposed the appraisal. A ministry wayhouse is suggested at Peakedge Song, and a mass pilgrimage might even allow its vallorn heart to be cleared.
